member.name: T:ILNumerics.Array`1
member.summary: The main n-dimensional, rectilinear array to be used in algorithms.
member.typeparam: Inner type. This will mostly be one of the predefined numeric types or one of the complex ILNumerics floating point types: and .
member.remarks:
This class serves as the main rectilinear array, holding arbitrary elements (usually numeric types or ) in arbitrary dimensions.
Arrays of this type may use any type as generic element. However, common mathematical functions and operators are defined for a limited number of value type elements only. All binary operations (+,-,*,/,<,>,<=,etc.) are defined for two arrays with the same numeric type, would it be from the System namespace (, , ...) or / . Most algebraic functions require floating point types. See the ILNumerics.ILMath class for a list of all computational functions.
Arrays are capable of creating flexible subarrays and are mutable at runtime. Read about all details of ILNumerics arrays in the ILNumerics Array documentation.
Arrays of this type are dense arrays. Cloning arrays is done as lazy copy on write, i.e.: clones of existing arrays do only use new memory when attempting to alter one of them. Arrays integrate into the memory management of ILNumerics. Read about the most important simple rules for using arrays in custom computational functions.
Arrays come with overloaded mathematical operators, allowing for a convenient syntax. A sophisticated memory management in the back will make sure, that as little memory is used as absolutely needed, even in non-trivial expressions, like: a + c * 2 / abs(sin(c) * -b / log(a)). Here all arrays are of the same or broadcastable size. Evaluating this expression does only need the memory of twice the size of one array. Memory gets collected and reused for every subexpression evaluation. Further optimization options exist, as described in Optimizing Algorithm Performance.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Array`1.op_Implicit(System.Array)~ILNumerics.Array{`0}
member.summary: Implicitly convert n-dimensional System.Array to ILNumerics array.
member.returns: If A is null: empty array. Otherwise a new ILNumerics array of the same size as A.
member.exception: If the type of the elements in A cannot get converted to .
If the type of the elements in A is not supported.

remarks.para: Elements of A will be copied to elements of the output array (shallow copy). The following element types are supported for and : double, float, int, uint, long, ulong, short, ushort, sbyte, byte.
Alternatively, may consists out of scalar Arrays (or InArray / OutArray) of one of the above element types.

The resulting Array will reflect all dimensions of A. Due to the fact that .NET System.Arrays are stored in row major order and ILNumerics stores array in column major (for compatibility with e.g. Matlab and Fortran) the resulting Array will have its dimensions reverted! For matrices this corresponds to a matrix transpose.

System.Convert is used for the conversion of elements in A to destination elements. This includes widening and narrowing conversions. When, for example, array elements of type double are provided and is Int32 the conversion will round the source elements. See the examples below.

example.code:
'' Elements of System.Value types: Dim A1 As Array(Of Double) = { 1, 2, 3 } ' provide int elements Dim A2 As Array(Of Double) = { 1.0, 2.9, 3.4, 5.12 } ' provide double elements Dim A As Double = 5 Dim B As Double = 6 Dim C As Double = 7
Dim A3 As Array(Of Double) = { A, B, C } ' provide double variables
Dim A4 As Array(Of Double) = { ILMath.cos(A), ILMath.tan(B) * C, C, 3 } ' provide mixed element types, including scalar Array

member.summary: This flag indicates that an array is not to be used anymore.

remarks.para: Since version 5 arrays implement multiple layers of reference counting and share their resources more frequently. Users shall not dispose arrays manually nor should there be any need to check for the life state of an array.

After an object was disposed (regardless of the reason, automatically or manually) it shall not be referenced anymore. A call to , thus, is only allowed for life arrays. On such arrays, always returns false, which makes this property a constant, semantically.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.BaseArray.ToStream(System.IO.Stream,System.String,ILNumerics.ArrayStreamSerializationFlags)
member.summary: Write values of this instance to a stream.
member.param: Stream to write the values into.
Format string to be used for output. See for a specification of valid formating expressions. This flag is only used, when 'method' is set to 'Serial'.
A constant out of . Specifies the way the values will be serialized.

remarks.para: If method 'Formatted' is used, any occurences of NewLine character(s) will be replaced from the format string before applying to the elements. This is done to prevent the format from breaking the 'page' style for the output.

If 'method' is set to 'Matlab', the array will be written as Matfile version 5.0. No compression will be used. The internal 'Name' property will be used as the array name for writing. This array instance will be the only array in the mat file. If you want to write several arrays bundled into one mat file, use the MatFile class to create a collection of arrays and write the MatFile to stream. Or use the classes in the ILNumerics.IO.HDF5 namespace to create a HDF5 format file (recommended).

member.summary: Convert input array (immutable) to local array (mutable).
member.returns: Local array with lifespan corresponding to the current scope.
member.remarks:
The new array is created from the source array and can be used multiple times in the function scope and get altered without modifying the source .
Array conversions in ILNumerics do not require new memory. Elements are not copied unless multiple arrays reference the same memory and one of them is about to be changed. Only then a copy of the memory is done and the change is performed on the copy (lazy copy on write).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Cell.Dispose
member.summary: Release this array after use. Cleans up on , and arrays which are not inside a block.

remarks.para: This method is used in rare situations where no artificial scope exists around the current function body. Examples of such situations are short snippets in anonymous- or lambda functions, entry methods, or intended manual memory management.

During 'normal' use the user places an artificial scope () around the function body. All , , and arrays created within the scope block are automatically tracked and released once the scope block is left.

Calling this method manually on local arrays as & Co. can be profitible in situations where no such scope block exists. Otherwise, the memory would be reclaimed at a later point in time by the GC. releases the array immediately. If no other arrays are sharing the same memory, it will be released to the memory pool for immediate recycling.

Note: failing to call in such situations does not create a memory leak! But the array is only reclaimed by the garbage collector and its memory is only freed by the finalization thread during the next GC collection. While this is considered regular use, disposing the array manually is recommended in situations where high performance execution or low memory consumption is required and no 'common' memory management is possible for some reasons.

Note further, that is not required in 'common' array uses. I.e. when dealing with inside existing scope blocks or when a return value is utilized in some way (incl. assignment to , calling member functions on the return value or giving the return value to other functions as input parameter).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.IndexIterator(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},System.Int64,System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders},System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: [Internal] Efficient iterator over the array for use in subarray evaluations.
member.param: Index of the last element in the dimension when the iterator is to be used in subarray operations.
[Optional] Determines the order the elements are walked along. Default: null ()
[Optional] Checks limits and throws an IOOR exception. Default: true (do perform checks).

[Optional] True: do not maintain features required for extended subarray-ing. Saves the determination [Optional] True: a volatile array type as source array will not be released after the itator finished enumerating s values. False: the iterator will release a volatile A (default). of out-of-range indices, NaN checks etc. The object returned will not provide all data! Default: false.
member.returns: Efficient, self destructing iterator instance, iterating over all elements of this array.
member.remarks: is used to enable the iterator for scenarios where error checking is performed outside of the iterator and focus is on speedy creation of the iterator. In subarray operations this is disabled and the more 'safe' variant is used. When enabled (true), no OOR checks are performed and is ignored.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.GetValue(ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.BaseArray})
member.summary: Retrieves a clone of the value of a scalar (0-dim) cell array as an array. Supports deep indexing.
member.returns: Copy/clone of the element value. Scalar arrays are wrapped into a scalar array.

remarks.para: This functions retrieves the value of the only element of a 0-dim scalar cell array.
The type of the array returned corresponds to the type of the element stored. Use in order to retrieve the element as its natural type. can be used to inspect the element type.

Note, that the value addressed is not wrapped into a scalar cell before returning as would be the case for indexers on cells, which always return cells. Thus the return value might be a cell or an ILNumerics array of any element type.

member.exception: if is not a 0-dimensional (numpy) scalar.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.SetValue``6(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},``0,System.Int64)
member.summary: Sets the value of the element addressed by .

remarks.para: This function replaces a single value of at the position as specified by the dimensional index .
is considered a sequential index into its own and into subsequent, merged dimensions (Matlab/ILNumericsV4 indexing style).

The function supports automatic expansion when addressing elements outside of the current dimension range. However, removal of parts of the array is not supported. Use the indexers defined on for removal operations in array style . It is recommended to initialize your arrays with a fixed size and to prevent from array size changing operations for best performance, though.

member.exception: if the expanded size as determined by the given indices is too large to be allocated.
if this array is currently in use by other arrays and locked against modifications. This should not happen during 'regular' use and may indicate a design flaw.
member.seealso: Subarray tutorial in the ILNumerics online documentation

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.SetValue(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{ILNumerics.BaseArray,ILNumerics.Cell,ILNumerics.InCell,ILNumerics.OutCell,ILNumerics.Cell,ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.CellStorage},ILNumerics.BaseArray)
member.summary: Sets the value of the scalar (0-dimensional) cell array .

remarks.para: This function replaces the only value of the 0-dimensional scalar array . It supports the deep-indexing feature on cell arrays. Regular arrays can be addressed by an index value 0 for virtual dimensions. In contrast to that indexing with integer values into cell arrays (deep indexing) requires exactly one index for each (non-virtual) dimension of every array addressed. Therefore, a 0-index overload exists for indexing into scalar (0-dim) cell arrays.

The function supports automatic expansion when addressing elements outside of the current dimension range. However, removal of parts of the array is not supported. Use the indexers defined on for removal operations in array style . It is recommended to initialize your arrays with a fixed size and to prevent from array size changing operations for best performance, though.

member.exception: if the expanded size as determined by the given indices is too large to be allocated.
if this array is currently in use by other arrays and locked against modifications. This should not happen during 'regular' use and may indicate a bad design.
member.seealso: Subarray tutorial in the ILNumerics online documentation.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.SetValue(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{ILNumerics.BaseArray,ILNumerics.Cell,ILNumerics.InCell,ILNumerics.OutCell,ILNumerics.Cell,ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.CellStorage},ILNumerics.BaseArray,System.Int64)
member.summary: Sets the value of the element addressed by . Supports deep indexing into cell elements.

remarks.para: This function replaces a single value of at the position as specified by the dimensional index .
is considered a sequential index into its own and into subsequent, merged dimensions (Matlab/ILNumericsV4 indexing style).

Deep indexing: the element to be replaced is located by matching the full set of given indices with the existing dimensions of the cell, starting with index . If the indices corresponding to the number of dimensions of this cell point to an ILNumerics array subsequent indices are used as indices into that array. On the other hand, if the element found is a cell, indexing is continued recursively at that cell element.

The function supports automatic expansion for existing dimensions of regular (non-cell) arrays. When the given indices address a non-existing element of a non-cell array the array currently stored in the cell is expanded in a way that the new value can be stored at the provided location of the array.

Removal of parts of the array is not supported. Use the indexers defined on for removal operations in array style . It is recommended to initialize your arrays with a fixed size and to prevent from array size changing operations for best performance, though.

member.exception: if the expanded size as determined by the given indices is too large to be allocated.
member.seealso: Subarray tutorial in the ILNumerics online documentation

member.param: [Optional] When true only non-infinity and non-NaN values will be considered as regular values. Default: false.

remarks.para: For complex values the real and imaginary parts of all elements are considered independently and the limits are returned separated in the real and imaginary parts of and .
The operation is efficiently performed on all elements of the input in a single run.
The operation is performed in multiple threads, according to the current settings of .
The input is not altered.

The function always succeeds and returns true for non-empty arrays of integer (non-floating point) element types. Overloads for floating point element types: the function succeeds on non-empty arrays which have at least one element other than NaN and / or 'Infinity' - depending on the setting of .

The optional parameter is useful, for example, to determine the minimum and maximum values stored inside this array in order to find scaling factors and for normalization purposes. Here, and can be ignored since they would be not useful as scaling factors. For the default value ('false') infinity values are considered regular values and contribute to the result.

For arrays of real element types ( and ) the value of the output parameters and is undefined if the function returns . For complex element types the individual parts of and determine the limits found among the real parts and among the imaginary parts. If limits could be computed for the real parts of the elements these limits will be stored into the real parts of and . Similarly, the limits among the imaginary elements are stored into the imaginary parts of and . If no limit could be computed (because all real or all imaginary element parts are all either NaN or Infinity (and was ) the corresponding part of and will be NaN.

member.summary: Tests if a cell element is of the given element type.
member.typeparam: The array element type to probe the cell element for.
member.param: Dimensional indices defining the position of the cell element to be probed.
member.returns: true if the element found at the given position is an array of the given element type , false otherwise.

remarks.para: The method is helpful in order to inspect the contents of a cell array. If the actual types of cells in the cell array are unknown this function can be used to determine the type of the content of individual cells before attempting to retrieve any values.

In most situations, elements of a cell are stored arrays of a distinct element type. That element type is given to as typeparameter . That means, in order to find out, if the first cell element stores an array of int cell.IsTypeOf<int>(0) is used.
When testing for arrays is used for .
In order to test for cell element type can be or : cell.IsTypeOf<BaseArray>(0).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.GetBaseArray(ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.BaseArray},System.Int64)
member.summary: Retrieves a clone of the value at the position as an array.
member.param: Index into the first dimension or sequential index into the array.
member.returns: Copy/clone of the elements value. Scalar values are wrapped into a scalar array.

remarks.para: This functions retrieves the value of the element at sequential index . Note that the index provided in does not correspond to the storage position of the element to retrieve. This would only be true for special cases of storage layout and dimension numbers. For arbitrary storage layouts both are likely to differ.
The type of the array returned corresponds to the type of the element addressed by . Use in order to retrieve the element as its natural type. can be used to inspect the element type.

Note, that the value addressed is not wrapped into a scalar cell before returning as would be the case for indexers on cells, which always return cells. Thus the return value might be a cell or an ILNumerics array of any element type. Commonly, the value returned will be a volatile return type array. Thus, it will be released after the first use.

member.exception: if the value of exceeds the of .

member.summary: [numpy API] Returns a single element from this array according to the provided dimension index.
member.param: Sequential index of the element to retrieve, as if the elements were stored in row-major order. -A.S.NumberOfElements <=d0<A.S.NumberOfElements.
member.returns: Copy of the element as located by the index argument .

remarks.para: An index for dimension i can be negative and must evaluate to an element position in the range 0...A.S[i]-1.

This function does support the merging of trailing, unspecified dimensions as known from GetValue(BaseArray{bool}, long, long). However, the element position is computed by assuming the elements to be laid-out sequentially in memory in row-major order. This function handles arbitrary storage orders, though, using its strides to compute the actual element position in memory.

member.returns: Copy of the element as located by the indices given by .

remarks.para: An index for dimension i can be negative and must evaluate to an element position in the range 0...A.S[i]-1, where negative indices count backwards, starting from the last element index in dimension i.
This function does not support the merging of trailing, unspecified dimensions as known from or from .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.put``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},ILNumerics.InArray{``0},ILNumerics.PutModes)
member.summary: [numpy API] Replaces elements of with at positions given by the sequential indices (flatten, row-major) .
member.typeparam: Element type of indices. Must be numeric.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be replaced.
Index array. The shape is ignored. Values must be numeric and are read in row-major order.
Values array. The shape is ignored. Values are read in row-major order.
[Optionl] Specifies how to handle index values in which are out-of-range. Default: error.

remarks.para: This function has a similar effect as doing A.flat[indices] = values in numpyInternal. However, in ILNumerics the iterator returned from A.flat is read-only. Use as a replacement.

Note that the values in are considered sequential indices, i.e. they correspond to the element position in a flattened array, where the flattening is performed in row-major order. For performance reasons and if . is not A is converted to row-major storage layout first and remains in row-major storage after the function returns. Note further, that the conversion happens proactively, and is not rolled back in case of errors during the iteration.
Elements of can be negative, which corresponds to indexing from the end of flattened .
Repeated values in lead to only the last corresponding value in to be stored at the respective position in .

If has more elements than are indices provided in superfluent values are ignored. No exception is thrown in this case. If has fewer elements than indices are provided in existing values are repeated as necessary.

The parameter determines what happens with indices laying outside of the bounds of A. The default value of throws an in this case. Two other options exist which bring the index back into the valid range: computes the modulus, limits the indices to the allowed range. Note that negative indices behave as usual (counting from the end of A) for modes and only.
requires the element type of to be value types (struct, commonly numeric).

member.exception: if is and any element in is out of the allowed range of [-A.S.NumberOfElements...>= A.].

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ExtensionMethods.repeat``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: [numpy API] Repeat elements along a flattened array or a specific axis.
member.typeparam: Element type of . Must be an integer type.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be repeated.
[Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) flatten A and repeat all values along dimension #0.

remarks.para: This function repeats elements of along a single dimension. By default, where no is defined is reshaped to a vector in row-major order and all elements are repeated according to . Otherwise, if an was specified, repetitions are performed along that dimension only. In this case, the array returned has the same shape as , except that the working dimension is enlarged.

The shape of is ignored. Its values give the counts for each element along the axis . Values must be numeric, positive integers and are read in row-major order. If has exactly one element all elements along the working dimension of are repeated by the same number. Alternatively, the length of must match A.S[axis] to specify individual repetition counts for each element along the working dimension. Thus, if is null (default) can be a scalar or an array with 'A.S.NumberOfElements == repeats.S.NumberOfElements'.
This function returns a new array and does not alter or any input parameters.

member.exception: if any of the or is null

remarks.para: This function repeats elements of along a single dimension. By default, where no is defined is reshaped to a vector in row-major order and all elements are repeated according to . Otherwise, if an was specified, repetitions are performed along that dimension only. In this case, the array returned has the same shape as , except that the working dimension is modified.
The value of gives the counts for each element along the axis . This value must be a positive integer.
This function returns a new array and does not alter or any input parameters.

if points to a virtual dimension; or if is negative.

This function internally creates a copy of . Therefore, the sorted values can be returned without significant overhead.

member.summary: [numpy API] Computes indices of maximum elements along the specified dimension of , recognizing NaNs.
member.param: Array to compute the indices for. This is not altered.
[Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) finds the maximum of the whole array.
[Optional] Returns the maximum values found from also. Default: (null) maximum values are not returned.

remarks.para: Negative dimension specifier '' will be shifted into the range of valid dimension indices. -1 corresponds to the last dimension.

prioritizes NaN values over non-NaN values. I.e.: if any of the elements is NaN the respective result value will be NaN also. Conversely, , ignores NaN values and gives the maximum among the non-NaN values, if possible. This corresponds to the behavior of ILNumerics version 4, Matlab(R) a.s.f.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.ToString
member.summary: Create textual description of this array. Limits the number of elements shown for very large arrays.
member.returns: String describing this array.

remarks.para: This function creates a textual representation of the array, describing the dimensionality, size and element values.

Elements of this array are displayed in a tabular form, corresponding to slices/subarrays of the whole array. Each table contains the elements along the first two dimension ( equal to ), or along the last two dimensions ( equal to ) respectively. Note, that a column major- or respective row major order representation is used according to the current setting of - the storage order of the array itself is not considered!

Very large arrays are abreviated so that no more than a certain number of elements are displayed per dimension. This is achieved by displaying elements at the beginning and at the end of a respective dimension only. Furthermore, a hard limit according to the value of applies. ILNumerics will try to respect this limit by limiting the number of elements displayed in any dimension. I.e. the value of is adjusted as necessary.

If this method is called on an array which is not yet fully configured (ILNumerics Virtual Processor) the function will halt and wait until configuration is finished and until all values become available. Use to allow inspecting unfinished array contents.
The display is optimized for common numeric element types.
This method is thread safe.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.ToString(System.UInt32,System.UInt32,System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders},System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a textual representation of this array and allows to control display parameters.
member.param: Maximum number of elements displayed for any dimension.
[Optional] Overall maximum number of elements displayed. Default: 10000. Use 0 to remove this limit.
[Optional] Show the elements in row major or column major order. Default: (i.e.: currently selected ArrayStyle).
[Optional] Add a header info with the element type. Default: true.
[Optional] Add a header info with the arrays size. Default: true.
[Optional] Controls the width of element columns (number of characters). Default: (auto, depends on type).
[Optional] true: automatically scale element values up / down for prettier display (default). False: do not scale element values.

[Optional] true: block execution until the content of this array is completely configured (default). False: generate info for intermediate state of this array, displays only such details, already configured.
member.returns: String with the content of this array converted according to the given parameters.

remarks.para: The function converts this array into a string for interactive display, for informal display and for utilization in interactive debug sessions.

Large arrays will be converted into a shorter form to save resources. The number of elements per dimension is limited to the value . Per default only 50 elements are shown from each dimension; 25 from the beginning and 25 from the end of each dimension. The value for may be adjusted to create smaller or larger output. 0 as value for removed the limit and shows all elements up to the number of .

The parameter limits the overall number of elements displayed, regardless of the actual dimension lengths. This parameter takes precedence over : if the array has too many dimensions and displaying all elements would exceed the number given by then the value of will automatically by adjusted (decreased) to keep the overall number of elements within the limits of .

0 as value for removes the limit of overall number of elements for the output. In order to display all elements of the array use ToString(0,0). Caution: for very large arrays this may use a lot of resources and may take long!

The elements of this array are displayed as "pages" or matrices. By default, and according to the current setting of these pages visualize slices of the array along the first and second dimension (). Or the pages are created from the last two dimensions (). The parameter allows to explicitly control if the display should follow row major or column major semantics.
The parameters and - if true - add a short info about the arrays size and type to the header (beginning) of the output.

allows to control the number of characters each element column of the output pages created will span. By default, this width is automatically adjusted. For most numeric element types this width is 12.

The signature of this function has been adjusted in version 5.4. The first parameter has been made [required]. The reason is that in some cases the overload resolution of the C# compiler has been observed to fail to prefer the parameterless version of over this function.
This method is thread safe. If elements of this array exist on non-host storage only, they will transparently be copied to the host memory.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.Dispose
member.summary: Releases this array after use. Cleans up on arrays which are no longer 'utilized'.

remarks.para: Note, that consequences of accessing an array variable or instance after was called on it are undefined. The array ('s storage) may immediately be reused for other arrays. It may be cleaned up, finalized, or reused in other computations. Hence, do not access the array after calling !

example.para: Here, we only access the output parameter I of the sort function. The array returned from sort(A, I) as the return value is not used, thus it is not released automatically. In order to free its resources immediately, one can call Dispose() on the returned array. Note, that no memory leak is produced without manually calling Dispose(). The array would be cleaned up by the GC instead. For best performance - even in debug mode - Dispose() can be called here.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.ReferenceCount
member.summary: Gets the number of arrays currently sharing the storage with this array.
member.remarks: Commonly, the number of array references for a storage is 1. Note, that ILNumerics implements a hierarchy of storage structures, each maintaining individual reference counters. Hence, a value of 1 does not guarantee or mean that no other arrays share the same memory. In fact, you should not rely on this property nor on its value. It may change at anytime and becomes immediately stale! ILNumerics manages references, disposal and copies automatically. Use this value for testing purposes only.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.ExportValues(`0[]@,ILNumerics.StorageOrders)
member.summary: (Expert API) Export (copy) values into System.Array.
member.param: System.Array with a copy of all element values from this array.
[Optional] The storage layout of the elements to write to .
member.remarks:
The System.Array can be predefined. If its length is sufficient, it will be used and its leading elements will be overwritten when function returns. If is null or has too few elements, it will be recreated from the _GC managed heap_.
Excessive use of this method can be a hint of suboptimal design! Especially if no array /no sufficiently long array is provided in the returned array will be created on the managed heap. This works around the ILNumerics memory management and may increases the pressure on the GC and can lead to frequent garbage collections and bad performance! Make sure to reuse the array .
If is null or the storage layout of this array will be used to store the elements into . Make sure that the array is large enough, even if the current storage layout corresponds to non-continously stored elements and may contain holes! Use to compute the absolute number of elements in necessary to hold all elements of this storage in its current storage order. Note further, that any potential holes in the element storage will not be cleared!
Exporting values of arrays gives a clone of the individual cell elements. Special care must be taken when working with arrays of type . Its use is not recommended! Failing to handle BaseArray instances properly may result in additional memory pressure, increased GC activation and unexpected when accessing (automatically) disposed BaseArray objects.
If - for some reasons - one needs to use on arrays nevertheless the following hints may serve as a rough guideline:
Objects returned in are return type objects or null. Return type objects will dispose their content and itself after the first use. Make sure to utilize each object exactly once!
Directly using an object in multiple times may give an error or unwanted side effects.
In order to work with or to access a returned object multiple times it must be (immediately) converted to a local array of the corresponding kind: , , or . This, if course, requires knowledge of the actual type of the object from within the cell.
Failing to use the array at least once may leaves references to other data arrays (memory handles) open. This may causes memory pressure on the GC and bad performance. However, in ILNumerics memory leaks (as for native languages) cannot happen.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.GetArrayForRead(ILNumerics.StorageOrders)
member.summary: Gets a copy of the array elements for read access.
member.param: [Optional] The order used for copying the elements into the returned System array. Default: .
member.returns: Managed System.Array with copies of the elements contained in this ILNumerics array.

remarks.para: This method is provided for experts only! Use this array only for reading! Changes will not populate back to the internal array storage. Note the default element storage format: column major.
Keep in mind, the length of the array may exceeds the number of elements!

The range of elements addresses by this ILNumerics array starts with index 0 of the returned. Any of this ILNumerics array is removed when copying the elements to the managed array. The internal elements will be read in .

The semantic of this method has changed with ILNumerics version 5. It now creates a copy of the internal elements in column major element storage order layout. The copy uses new memory from the regular, GC managed heap. This fact and the required memory copy introduce a computational effort which disqualifies this method for high performance algorithms.
The recommended way for experts to access internal elements directly, is now, to acquire a pointer to the memory and to use the pointer in your unsafe code.
In order to save the allocation of the managed array returned, consider using the method .
The parameter allows to control the order of the elements returned. Valid values are and . The default value is .

This method is now partly obsolete but it will remain here since it serves its purpose still: by copying the elements one enables compatibility with other .NET APIs, at the same time it ensures that the values returned will still be around and will not be affected by the cleanup mechanisms all internal array storage is subject of. BUT: note the size limitation all in .NET undergo! Attempts to acquire the elements of such arrays which exceed the maximum sizes of .NET objects will trigger an exception.
The former versions (< 5) method 'GetArrayForWrite()' has been replaced by Array{T}.GetHostPointerForWrite(StorageOrders).
This method is thread safe.

member.exception: if is none of column major or row major.
if this array is too large to fit into a managed array or if there is not enough memory currently available to allocate the return array.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.GetHostPointerForRead(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: [Expert API - UNSAFE!] Acquire a read pointer to the memory storing the first element of this array.
member.param: [Optional] Ensures that the array is in a specific storage layout before acquiring the pointer. Default: (null) don't change the storage layout.
member.returns: Pointer to the first element of this array.
member.remarks:
This function returns a pointer to the first element stored in this array. Any base offset configured for the array is taken into account. The pointer points to the memory used by this array directly - not to a copy of this memory!
Do not use this pointer for modifying the value of an element of this array! This pointer is for read purposes only!
For empty arrays A (where A. is true) the value of the pointer returned is undefined.
This pointer is valid only as long as this array is not modified or released! Do not attempt to use this pointer after the array has been released, ran out of the current scope (meaning the current function scope as well as ), or is modified!
The order of elements in this array is determined by the size descriptor . Use the strides, dimension lengths and the size of the elements () in order to compute the byte offset to individual elements relative to this pointer.
The memory region addressed by the pointer returned exists on the unmanaged heap. Hence, it does not need to be pinned and will not be moved by the GC. However, this memory is subject of deterministic disposal, pooling and frequent reuse by other arrays. Do not use the pointer returned after this array left the current function scope, was modified, reassigned or released!
When is not null the storage order of the array is modified according to . Valid values for are , , and null. The parameter can be convenient in order to access elements of non-continous array layouts. Instead of computing the address of individual elements (, or ) the array can be brought into a continous storage layout before acquiring the pointer. Afterwards, elements can be accessed sequentially in memory, with unity strides. The price is the rearranging of the whole storage which commonly requires a copy of all elements.
This function may imply a copy operation from device specific memory onto host memory. This copy - if required - will be performed transparently to the user. The copy is done synchronously, i.e.: when the function returns the pointer returned will be valid. The user is not required to wait for asynchronous operations.
member.exception: if called on a return type array or if the elements are not of a .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.Equals(System.Object)
member.summary: Test if this array equals another array.
member.returns: True if the element type, all element values and dimension sizes match, false otherwise.

remarks.para: The comparison returns true if both arrays are of the same type, have the same shape and if all element values match.

Note, that the of the arrays is not considered for the comparison. This way it is perfectly legal for two arrays to return true while one array is stored in, let's say: and the other array is ordered along the rows (). However, all elements at matching sequencial positions / with matching indices in the flattened array must equal in order to return true.

Singleton dimensions are ignored. As one consequence, and accept two vectors even if the orientations do not match. A row vector with the same element values than another column vector of the same lengths are considered to be equal to each other.

para.b: This function returns true for empty arrays of the same shape and element type. It always returns true when used on an array with itself as parameter .

remarks.para: Comparing of type as returns true if this array is scalar (i.e.: it has exactly one element) and the value of the only element equals the value of the provided scalar.

For floating point element types the comparison is made on the byte-level. Thus, only exact matches are considered 'equal'. Therefore, this function is not intended to compare the results of such floating point operations which are subject of rounding errors. Consider computing the absolute distance of both floating point results instead and compare this to the eps value of the floating point data type with appropriate precision and scaling.
values are never equal to itself or any other value.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.GetHashCode
member.summary: Generate a hash code based on the current values.
member.returns: Hash code
member.remarks:
The hashcode is created by taking the values currently stored in the array into account. Therefore, the function iterates over all elements in the array - which makes it somehow an expensive operation. Take this into account if you consider using large arrays in collections like dictionaries or hash tables, which make great use of such hash codes.
This method is thread safe.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.Detach
member.summary: Detaches the buffer set hosting the array elements from this array if they are shared with other storages. Afterwards, this array uses its own, dedicated memory.

remarks.para: This method is thread safe in that the buffer set _currently_ attached to this array is detached from other storages, potentially also using the same buffer set. However, the storage might be changed or even substituted concurrently by operations accessing the same array on other threads. Hence, while the storage this function works on will be detached after the function returns it may no longer belongs to this array. Locking or other synchronization methods can be used to handle this case.

Note further, that calling does not ensure exclusive access to the arrays memory. The arrays' storage may be used / accessed from other threads concurrently and changes to it will be visible to such users immediately.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.AsReadOnlySpanInternal(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: Returns a span providing access to this array's internal storage for reading.
member.param: [Optional] The order of elements returned. If order is null (default) the current value of is assumed, which depends on .
member.returns: A span with the exact length needed to hold all elements of this array, referencing the elements of this array, and having the same lifetime as this array.

remarks.para: Depending on the current internal storage layout this array is reordered internally as required before returning the span representing the elements in the requested storage order.

Note, that for returning an array as span it must be ensured that the arrays elements are layed-out continously in memory. Thus, the requested storage order is enforced in advance. This may or may not involve an internal copy of the elements of this array and a (transparent to the user) modification in its storage layout.
The Span returned references the same memory as this array. No copy is made.
The Span returned is only valid as long as this array is alive and before a subsequent modification is performed to this array.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.T_get(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{`0,`1,`2,`3,`4,`5})
member.summary: Returns transposed version of this array.
member.remarks:
For matrices, this swaps columns with rows. For arrays, the dimensions are shifted by one.
Note, for complex elements, no conjugate is created! Use conj(A.T) if this is intended.
The storage format of the array returned depends on the original storage format. Matrices stored in column major format will produce row major matrices and vice versa. Note that the storage format for vectors (1 dimensional arrays) will not change since it is the same for both formats.
This method is thread safe.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray`6.op_Addition(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{`0,`1,`2,`3,`4,`5},ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{`0,`1,`2,`3,`4,`5})
member.summary: Elementwise addition operator on two numeric arrays.
member.returns: Array with result of A + B, with element type T.

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

This function is parallelized for multiple cores. If possible, a suitable or is directly utilized in order to perform the operation inplace: instead of storing the results into new memory the input array and/or its storage is reused and returned.
T must be a numeric value type, including and .

It is convenient when subarrays are to be created without knowing the number of dimensions and the concrete range parameters in advance. It is not recommended for situations where high performance is crucial. Note, that individual objects for each dimension addressed in can be used in exactly one call to and are released in the function automatically. Thus, when calling in loops make sure to recreate all dimension specifier prior to each call to .

Note, that the array returned may use the same element storage as this array in this case. Only when trying to modify either one of this array or the subarray a copy will be made. More complex subarray specifications may require iterating and copying addressed elements into new memory.
The setting (as controlled by ) is respected for the array returned.

This overload of Subarray() allows to define range specifiers for individual dimensions as a system array. It is convenient when subarrays are to be created without knowing the number of dimensions and the concrete range parameters in advance. It is not recommended for situations where high performance is crucial. Note, that individual objects for each dimension addressed in can be used in exactly one call to and are released in the function automatically. Thus, when calling in loops make sure to recreate all dimension specifier prior to every call to .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.GetHostPointerForWrite(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: [Expert API - UNSAFE!] Acquire a writable pointer to the memory location storing the value of the first element of this array.
member.returns: Pointer to the first element of this array.
member.remarks:
This function returns a pointer to the first element stored in this array. Any base offset configured for the array is taken into account. The pointer points to the memory used by this array directly - not to a copy of this memory!
For empty arrays ( is true) the value of the pointer returned is undefined.
This pointer is valid immediately, after the function returns. It remains valid until the next use of this array or until the end of the current scope block. Do not attempt to use this pointer after the array has been used, released, ran out of scope, was reassigned or is modified!
Keep in mind that any use of an array - would it be for reading, for writing, when using the array as parameter in array function calls, etc. - potentially and transparently alters the internal array structures. Hence, using the array in any of such ways may invalidates the pointer acquired. Using such invalidated pointer results in undefined behavior, including writing to invalid memory and/or crashing the application.
In a multithreading setup and when the array hosting the memory to write to is shared with other threads manual synchronization (f.e.: locking) is required. It is recommended to use a clone of the arrays before providing it to another thread.
The order of elements in this array is determined by the size descriptor . Use the strides, dimension lengths and the size of the elements
in order to compute the byte offset to individual elements relative to this pointer.
The memory region addressed by the pointer returned exists on the unmanaged heap for numeric element types. Hence, it does not need to be pinned and will not be moved by the GC. However, this memory is subject of deterministic disposal, pooling and frequent reuse by other arrays. Do not use the pointer returned after this array left the current function scope, was modified, reassigned or released!
Since ILNumerics' memory management does transparently perform 'lazy copies on write' calling this function may cause the underlying memory to be copied - transparently as well. Therefore, do not call this function unless you really want to change the memory addressed. For reading purposes it is cheaper to acquire a pointer via: . Latter option is available not only for (as ), but on any non-volatile array, including input and output arrays.
works for element types of (structs in C#) only. The behavior for reference types ('class' elements) is undefined.
member.exception: if called on a return type array or if the elements are not of a .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.AsSpan(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: Returns a span providing access to this array's internal storage for reading and writing.
member.param: [Optional] The order of elements returned. If order is null (default) the current value of is assumed, which depends on .
member.returns: A span with the exact length needed to hold all elements of this array, referencing the elements of this array, and having the same lifetime as this array.

remarks.para: Depending on the current internal storage layout this array is reordered internally as required before returning the span representing the elements in the requested storage order.

Note, that for returning an array as span it must be ensured that the arrays elements are layed-out continously in memory. Thus, the requested storage order is enforced in advance. This may or may not involve an internal copy of the elements of this array and a (transparent to the user) modification in its storage layout.
When called on a mutable array type the span returned can be used to alter elements of this array via the Span<T>.
The Span returned is only valid as long as this array is alive and before a subsequent modification is performed to this array.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.AsReadOnlySpan(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: Returns a span providing access to this array's internal storage for reading.
member.param: [Optional] The order of elements returned. If order is null (default) the current value of is assumed, which depends on .
member.returns: A span with the exact length needed to hold all elements of this array, referencing the elements of this array, and having the same lifetime as this array.

remarks.para: Depending on the current internal storage layout this array is reordered internally as required before returning the span representing the elements in the requested storage order.

Note, that for returning an array as span it must be ensured that the arrays elements are layed-out continously in memory. Thus, the requested storage order is enforced in advance. This may or may not involve an internal copy of the elements of this array and a (transparent to the user) modification in its storage layout.
The Span returned is only valid as long as this array is alive and before a subsequent modification is performed to this array.

Using a read-only span allows to read from the underlying memory of this array - even while this memory may be shared with other arrays. Thus, saving from 'detaching' the array and from a memory copy makes using read-only span preferrable over when no modifications to element values are required.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.shape
member.summary: [numpy API] The dimension lengths as ILNumerics vector of length corresponding to .

remarks.para: This property allows to query the dimension lengths as an ILNumerics vector. The vector returned will have at least () one dimension with the dimension lengths of this array as elements. Numpy scalars return an empty vector.

For mutable arrays the shape can also be changed inplace by assigning to this property. Changing the shape is only allowed for mutable arrays which are in a suitable state: the storage must be continously layed out, the number of elements must not change.
Immutable arrays do not expose a setter property / function for the shape attribute.

member.exception: if this array is currently shared with multiple instance. For example, if it is in use by an instance of as function parameter and the function has not returned yet. Applying the ILNumerics function rules prevent from such situations commonly.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.strides
member.summary: [numpy API] The strides of elements within the dimensions. Unit: element size.
member.remarks:
Elements within a dimension of ILNumerics arrays are separated in memory by a certain, fixed address offset. This offset is the same for all elements within the same dimension. The array returned gives this offset for each dimension of this array.
Note that the unit of the distance is the element size, i.e. the number of bytes consumed by a single element. In difference to that, the numpy attribute gives this distance in bytes.
This attribute is readonly.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.ndim
member.summary: [numpy API] The number of dimensions stored for this array.

remarks.para: This readonly attribute is an alias for .

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.data
member.summary: [numpy API][Expert API!] Gives a reference to the memory handle used to store elements of this array on the host.

remarks.para: The memory handle returned gives access to the memory used to store the arrays data. In order to read and/or write from / to this memory one must take many considerations into account, including but not limited to: ,,, handle type, element type, , , . Failing to do so may result in memory access violations and/or in corrupted objects.

Handling with memory handles directly is inherently unsafe! Neither the ILNumerics API nor the .NET CLR will prevent you from doing wrong! Therefore, this API is for expert users only. You have been warned and you are on your own!
The handle returned will be a for elements and a for reference type . Latter, in general live on the managed heap while former address unmanaged heap process memory. Good luck!

member.exception: when no handle is attached to the hast memory for this array.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.size_
member.summary: [numpy API] Gives the number of elements in this array. This attribute is an alias for . [readonly]

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.nbytes
member.summary: [numpy API] The total number of bytes required to store all elements of this array. [readonly]
member.remarks: The number returned counts the bytes for the elements of the array only. It does not take into account the memory used for non-element fields and attributes. Also, may not be a measure for the overall size of the memory region actually _used_ to store the elements. This region might be larger if elements are non-contiguously laid-out in memory.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.itemsize
member.summary: [numpy API] The number of bytes required to store a single element in memory. [readonly]
member.remarks: The number of bytes for a single element mostly correspond to the sizeof(T1) operator in C# for numeric types. One exception are the elements of arrays which consume only 1 byte, while sizeof(bool) typically equals: 4. can be seen as a more general variant of 'sizeof(T1)', taking these subtleties into account.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.flat
member.summary: Readonly iterator over the elements of this array in row-major order.
member.returns: Iterator object.

remarks.para: The returned allows to iterate over the elements of an array A as if 'A.flatten' was called first. Iteration goes along the rows (last dimension indices varying fastest).

Note that in difference to numpys 'flatiter' objects, the source array cannot be changed via the iterator. For assigning to elements consider utilizing a size iterator to acquire an iterator over the element offsets in memory and use Array{T1}.SetValue(T1, long) or Array{T}.GetHostPointerForWrite(StorageOrders?) to write to the memory.
is defined for reference type elements and for all numeric value type element arrays.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.Item(System.Int64)
member.summary: Retrieves the value(s) of the element(s) at the position(s) specified by or sets them.
member.param: Index into the first dimension or sequential index into the array.
member.returns: Element value(s) wrapped into a new array.
member.value: Right side array with value(s) to be assigned to the element(s) addressed.

remarks.para: This functions retrieves/ modifies an individual element or a subarray corresponding to .

If this array has more dimensions than indices specified the size of the subarray returned / of the subarray addressed depends on the setting of . For is considered a sequential index into its own and into subsequent, merged dimensions. The array returned will be a scalar. This mode allows to expand / to remove parts of this array when using the set accessor.

For all indices must fit into their dimensions. Any unspecified trailing dimensions are substituted with and the array returned may contain multiple elements from those dimensions. does not allow to change the size of existing arrays.

This indexer is readonly on immutable types. It is optimized for efficient single element access by providing a distinct index parameter for each dimension of this array. Providing a number of indices matching the number of dimensions in this array is recommended for speed and for compatibility of the index access with both .

In order to access elements based on their element type directly (i.e.: without wrapping it into a new array) and as a faster alternative for scalar or mostly-scalar algorithms use one of the extension methods or similar overloads for concrete arrays.
This overload allows indexing into huge arrays and negative indices, addressing elements from the end of their respective dimension / merged dimensions.

member.exception: if the value of exceeds the .
member.seealso: Subarray tutorial in the ILNumerics online documentation

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable`6.a
member.summary: Assign another array to this array variable. This is an optional, yet more efficient alternative to using '=' for assigning to the array directly.
member.remarks: By using this method, the storage of this array is immediately released to the memory pool and replaced by the new arrays content. In difference to that, by using the common '=' assignment operator, the existing arrays storage is released only at the time, the current block is left. Therefeore, prefer this method if a smaller memory pool is crucial.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.shape
member.summary: [numpy API] The dimension lengths as ILNumerics vector of length corresponding to .

remarks.para: This property allows to query the dimension lengths as an ILNumerics vector. The vector returned will have at least () one dimension with the dimension lengths of this array as elements. Numpy scalars return an empty vector.

For mutable arrays the shape can also be changed inplace by assigning to this property. Changing the shape is only allowed for mutable arrays which are in a suitable state: the storage must be continously layed out, the number of elements must not change.
Immutable arrays do not expose a setter property / function for the shape attribute.

member.exception: if this array is currently shared with multiple instance. For example, if it is in use by an instance of as function parameter and the function has not returned yet. Applying the ILNumerics function rules prevent from such situations commonly.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.strides
member.summary: [numpy API] The strides of elements within the dimensions. Unit: element size.
member.remarks:
Elements within a dimension of ILNumerics arrays are separated in memory by a certain, fixed address offset. This offset is the same for all elements within the same dimension. The array returned gives this offset for each dimension of this array.
Note that the unit of the distance is the element size, i.e. the number of bytes consumed by a single element. In difference to that, the numpy attribute gives this distance in bytes.
This attribute is readonly.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.ndim
member.summary: [numpy API] The number of dimensions stored for this array.

remarks.para: This readonly attribute is an alias for .

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.size_
member.summary: [numpy API] Gives the number of elements in this array. This attribute is an alias for . [readonly]

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.nbytes
member.summary: [numpy API] The total number of bytes required to store all elements of this array. [readonly]
member.remarks: The number returned counts the bytes for the elements of the array only. It does not take into account the memory used for non-element fields and attributes. Also, may not be a measure for the overall size of the memory region actually _used_ to store the elements. This region might be larger if elements are non-contiguously laid-out in memory.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.itemsize
member.summary: [numpy API] The number of bytes required to store a single element in memory. [readonly]
member.remarks: The number of bytes for a single element mostly correspond to the sizeof(T1) operator in C# for numeric types. One exception are the elements of arrays which consume only 1 byte, while sizeof(bool) typically equals: 4. can be seen as a more general variant of 'sizeof(T1)', taking these subtleties into account.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Immutable`6.flat
member.summary: Readonly iterator over the elements of this array in row-major order.
member.returns: Iterator object.

remarks.para: The returned allows to iterate over the elements of an array A as if 'A.flatten' was called first. Iteration goes along the rows (last dimension indices varying fastest).

Note that in difference to numpys 'flatiter' objects, the source array cannot be changed via the iterator. For assigning to elements consider utilizing a size iterator to acquire an iterator over the element offsets in memory and use Array{T1}.SetValue(T1, long) or Array{T}.GetHostPointerForWrite(StorageOrders?) to write to the memory.
is defined for reference type elements and for all numeric value type element arrays.

member.summary: Retrieves the value(s) of the element(s) at the position(s) specified by . Deep indexing for cells.
member.param: Index into the first dimension or sequential index into the array.
member.returns: Element value wrapped into a new scalar array.

remarks.para: This functions retrieves the value of the element at sequential index . Note that the index provided in does not correspond to the storage position of the element to retrieve. This would only be true for special cases of storage layout and dimension numbers. For arbitrary storage layouts both are likely to be different.

This indexer is readonly on immutable types. The get accessor returns a scalar array. In order to receive the value of the element addressed as system type directly (i.e.: without wrapping it into a new array) and as a faster alternative for scalar or mostly-scalar algorithms use and/or its specific overloads for the individiual element types.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Global.Helper.BC_prepareIterationDims``2(ILNumerics.Size,ILNumerics.Size,System.Int64*,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Prepares all dimension and strides array for efficient iteration in binary, broadcasting operators.
member.typeparam: Element type. Used to determine the element size / strides.
Output element type. Used to determine strides.
member.param: Input / output: predefined array with dimension lengths. Output: holds dimension lengths and strides, ready for iteration.
True: reverses the dimensions / strides of the returned BSD.

remarks.para: This functions takes the dimension lengths in and completes the buffer with * out strides, * A strides and * B strides for binary operator iteration.
All strides are multiplied with the element size of in bytes.
All dims are decreased by 1 for easier iteration later.

is of minimum length 3 + 7 * 4, for [ndims, nelem, offs] + outdims + outstrides ++ stridesA ++ stridesB. On entry, only elements 0, 1 and 3...[ndims-1] are expected. other info (strides) are completed and returned within this function.
If is true all dimensions and strides are reversed. This corresponds to an output array in row major order.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Global.Helper.PrepareBSD4WriteTo(ILNumerics.Size,System.Int64*,System.UInt32,System.Int64*)
member.summary: creates the bsd and strides for fast iteration in WriteTo functions
member.param: temp BSD / dim / strides for iteration. This is expected to be at least of len: ndims * 3 + 3 for: (out)ndims, nelem, baseoffset, dims, strides, (in) strides

remarks.para: This function prepares the strides for iterating over the output elements of the destination array efficiently:
1) Dimensions are reordered to iterate along the dimension of the destination array with the smallest strides.
2) virtual dimensions in inSize are replaced with singleton dimensions, so that the number of dimensions in inSize equals ndims of outSize.
3) all singleton dimensions in inSize get a stride of 0 assigned.
4) broadcasting is allowed on the right side only!

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Misc.QuickSort.QuickSortAscST(System.Double*,System.Int64,System.Int64,System.Int64)
member.summary: One dimensional quick sort, inline, ascending, arbitrary element spacing
member.param: data array, 1dim, replaced on output with sorted values

remarks.para: Quick sort algorithm is used for ranges of minimum lengths specified by and above. Below that length, a simple insertion sort is used instead.

The algorithm implements a non-recursive quicksort variant. Therefore a small amount of memory is needed to perform the sorting. That 'stack' memory is preserved from the ILMemoryPool. The size is determined by the value of .

Handling of NaN values (for double,float,complex or fcomplex arrays element datatypes only): if the input array contains any NaN values, those elements will be sorted to the end of the array on output.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.DeviceManagement.HostDevice.New``1(System.UInt64,System.Boolean,ILNumerics.PoolSizePolicy,System.UInt64)
member.summary: Acquire a memory handle / array from this pool or create a new one. This class allows to be a reference type.
member.typeparam: Type of elements which will be stored in the memory.
member.param: Number of elements. This determins the size of the memory required.
[Optional] True: clear the element values. False: do not clear the elements (default).
[Optional] Allocation policy: regular (default) or segmented mode (limited).
[Optional] if set, gives the number of typed elements, considering the element byte length - for untyped allocations.
member.returns: A referencing a region of main (virtual) memory sufficient to store elements of type .

remarks.para: The allocates arrays for elements on native process memory instead on the managed heap. Reference type elements, however, are allocated on the managed heap. Hence, the handle returned will either be a or a . Note, both categories of memory are managed in their own pools. In the case of elements and native storage the new memory will - if possible - be taken from the pool associated with the current thread and the host device. For managed arrays the global, static, thread local pool is considered.

member.summary: General operator over elements of , not inplace. Potentially other output type.
member.returns: New scalar array.

remarks.para: The operation is efficiently performed on all elements of the input array .

The storage order of the array returned depends on the order of . If . is true the array returned will have the same as . Otherwise, the elements of the returned array will be reordered in the order defined by (default: ).
The operation is performed in multiple threads, according to the current settings of .
The input array is not altered. However, if 's storage is suitable and not shared by other arrays its memory will be used for the result and the operation is performed 'inplace'.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.flip(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt32},System.Int32)

member.param: [Optional] Index of the working dimension or -1 for determining the working dimension automatically (default).

This method is implemented for all common numeric element types, including and logical arrays.
This function may works inplace and may returns the same instance of .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.max(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the maximum of elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] True: reduced singleton dimension is not removed from the output (default). False: the new singleton dimension is removed.
The index of the dimension to be reduced.
[Optional] Output: 0-based index values of the found elements along the working dimension. Default: (null) don't return the indices.
member.returns: New array with the same shape as except that the dimension specified by is reduced to length min(1,A.S[dim]) and removed if is false.

remarks.para: Empty arrays are handled in the same way as other shapes: the dimension specified by is reduced to 1. If A.S[dim] == 0 the s dimension length in the array returned will also be 0.
Scalar arrays: numpy scalars give a numpy scalar (0 dim) as output.

Special floating point values (for floating point element types): positive and negative infinity are handled in the regular way. NaN ('not a number') values are ignored. If all elements in a working dimension are NaN, NaN is returned as result in the corresponding output element.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If is null on entry (default) no indices are computated (may or may not decreasing the computational effort of completing this function).

Stability: if is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same minimum/maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined. It may point to the first or any other element storing the smallest / largest value returned from the working dimension. Thus, Min() and Max() are unstable regarding the index output argument!

member.exception: If A.S[dim] == 0 and was false.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.xor(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'Xor' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.summary: Binary, elementwise, broadcasting apply<T1,T2,long,Tout>(A,B). Maps a scalar operation from elements of and to a third array, provides element index. Arbitrary types. Parallelized.
member.param: The elementary (scalar) function to be used to perform the operation on corresponding elements of and , utilizing respective element values and the index used to locate the output array in iteration order.
member.returns: New or reused array with result of operating elements of and elementwise.

remarks.para: The iteration order depends on the order of input arrays: for column major input i will run in column major order and in row major order for row major inputs. If inputs have other, undefined or different storage orders the result is undefined. It is recommended to use this function on vector input(s) or with a well defined storage order for inputs and/or .
This function may automatically work inplace on either of both input parameters, if possible.

example.para: 'Merge' elements a of an vector of 0's with a scalar -1, weighting with the location index i by applying the function: c = a + i * b.
Efficiently overwrite/initialize the content of an uninitialized array with upwards counting values, row major storage order.

The last example produces the same result as the expression: counter(4,3,2, StorageOrders.RowMajor);. The larger flexibility in the generator function comes with a slight computational overhead, though.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.eq(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Elementwise 'EqualTo' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.neq(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'UnEqualTo' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.param: [Optional] number of fractional digits to round to. Default: (0) round to integers.
member.returns: Array of same size as A with elements of A rounded towards the nearest even integer value.

remarks.para: The operation is efficiently performed on all elements of the input array .

The storage order of the array returned depends on the order of . If . is true the array returned will have the same as . Otherwise, the elements of the returned array will be reordered in the order defined by (default: ).
The operation is performed in multiple threads, according to the current settings of .
The input array is not altered. However, if 's storage is suitable and not shared by other arrays its memory will be used for the result and the operation is performed 'inplace'.
