member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.cell(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{ILNumerics.BaseArray},ILNumerics.StorageOrders)
member.summary: Creates new cell, initialize size and provide arrays for cell elements.
member.param: [Optional] Size hint for the new cell array. Default: (null) Derive the size from .
[Optional] Enumerable of arrays for the cell elements, column major order. Default: (null) creates cell with all 'null' elements.
[Optional] Storage order for the new cell. Default: .
member.returns: Cell of specified size, initialized with given arrays.

remarks.para: If number of arrays given is smaller than the number of elements given by then trailing elements in the cell returned are set to null.
If is null a cell vector is produced with a length corresponding to the number of elements in . Performance wise it is recommended to specify the explicitly, though.
If contains more elements than expected by an error is generated.
The function or one of its overloads are convenient for the specification of dimensional size arguments.
Visit the online documentation for cell.

Note that when is an ILNumerics array (as in the example where was created by the function) memory management is performed accordingly: arrays stored in the object are released and the associated memory is released to the pool after the function returns. However, for of other (non-ILNumerics) types proper memory management is not guaranteed. For example, when providing the target cell element values in a of a copy of individual elements is made by the function before storing the new element into the cell object. The source object remains an element of the system array and is not released!

Therefore, in situations where performance is critical and inside loops use one of the ILNumerics array intialization functions for providing the argument. Otherwise, temporary objects in the may remain live and are left for the GC to clean up (which is fine, except for high performance demands).

member.example: Array A = rand(10,20,30); Cell C = cell(size(3,2),vector(A, A+1, zeros(2,3), "4th element")); //Alternatives: //Cell C = cell(size(3,2),new [] { A, A+1, zeros(2,3) }); //Cell C = cell(size(3,2),row(A, A+1, zeros(2,3))); C >Cell [3,2] > [0]: > [1]: { [10,20,30]} { [1,1]} > [2]: { [10,20,30]} {null} > [3]: { [2,3]} {null}
member.exception: if is not null and the number of elements found in exceeds the expected number of elements as specified by .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.cell(ILNumerics.BaseArray[],System.Int32[])
member.summary: Create cell, initialize with arrays and size.
member.param: Predefined system array with ILNumerics arrays as elements to be stored into the new cell.
Size of the new cell array.
member.returns: Cell with size of and elements from

remarks.para: The arrays given in are stored into the new cell as individual cell elements. As for all cell elements, a (lazy) clone is made prior to storing the arrays into the cell. Therefore, the arrays are properly protected from changes from outside the cell.
This function is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Consider using instead which does not rely on params arguments.

remarks.para: The function and the corresponding overloads for providing individual dimension length parameters ,... create n-dimensional numeric arrays with automatically generated values based on a given value and a value. The size of the new array is determined by the parameter(s). The firsts element value is assigned the value. Subsequent values are computed by adding the value of to each elements predecessor.

The term 'predecessor' here means: the predecessor E0 of element E1 is the element having an index I(E0) of I(E1) - 1, where the index I() corresponds to the storage location of the element in memory, relative to the first element.

The storage order is determined by . By default, elements are lined up in memory in column major storage order. must be one out of or . Note, how the storage order affects the order of values in the new array.

example.para: Creating a new array of size [4,3], filled with upwards counting values, starting at 1.
Creating a new array of size [4,3,2] of ushort values:
Note, how the computed values of data type 'sbyte' wrap around at the limits of 'sbyte' without notice!
Creating a new array of size [4,3] with upwards counting values in row major order:

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.New``1(System.UInt64,System.UInt32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Provides memory / T[] / a device buffer for the current thread. This is for expert users and rare low-level scenarios only. Use the common array creation functions instead!
member.typeparam: Element type, specifies the type and size of elements.
member.param: Number of elements which must at least fit into the memory region.
[Optional] Index of the device owning the memory. Default: 0 is the host device.
[Optional] Flag determining whether the memory should be initialized to zero. Default: do not clear.
member.returns: The returned will be a to a region on the main (virtual) memory, a to the managed heap or a on an OpenCL device.

remarks.para: This function attempts to acquire the requested chunk of memory from the memory pool of the specified device. Only if no matching region was found, memory is allocated from the low level allocation functions offered by the device.

This function supports the utilization of memory regions in a C style manner: user have to manage memory explicitly and manually. Instead of using this function it is recommended to use the common ILNumerics array creation functions to create and work with ILNumerics arrays. which do not require to create, clean up or to pool memory manually. ILNumerics function rules do all this automatically. Thus, manual memory management is left to a few, very specific situations only.

Depending on the type category the memory handle returned references one of the following memory types:
T is struct / ValueType: memory is allocated on the unmanaged heap. There is no inherent size limitation. Access to the memory is done by means of the property. Users are responsible to correctly deal with such pointers. All risks of unsafe code apply.
T is class / reference type: the function allocates an .NET on the managed heap. Access is done by first casting the memory handle returned to the concrete type of and then using the property to acquire the T[] array.
if is greater than 0 the handle returned may be a buffer to an OpenCL device. For shared virtual memory devices (SVM), however, such buffers will be backed with a corresponding region of memory on the native virtual memory manager managed heap. It is this complexity which leads to the suggestion to not use this method of manual memory management ('New' and 'free') unless really necessary and unless you know what you are doing.
Attempting to access the on a native handle generates an exception.
Attempting to access the on a ManagedHostHandle{T} generates an exception.

MemoryHandles are critical handles. Disposal is guaranteed by critical execution regions and the GC. However, users should dispose the handle to free the memory region immediately after use. Use for disposing memory handles.

member.exception: on failed attempts to allocate a memory region on the specified device.

member.summary: Reinterpret the elements of A as elements of type . Expand or shrink the array size accordingly.
member.returns: A new array with the element type , referencing the same memory as A.
member.remarks:
The cast is performed regardless of the way the individual elements of A are currently stored in memory. When using this method one must consider the endianness of the system, which can vary from machine to machine!
If is of equal size as the array returned will have the same size and striding as A.
If the size of is smaller than the size of multiple elements of A are collapsed into a corresponding output element. Both sizes must match so that multiple element instances of fit exactly into a single element. The dimension where elements in A are stored continously in memory is shrinked by the fraction of the element size difference.
Otherwise, if the input elements size is larger than the size of a new trailing dimension is added, containing the newly extracted component from the larger input elements. In this case, the array returned has the same size than A, padded with a trailing dimension and the new dimension's length equals the number of fitting exactly into .
member.exception: if the sizes of the types requested do not match or if the storage layout of A is not appropriate.

member.returns: pairwise L1 distances between the data point provided in the input vector and the data points stored in the matrix .

This function is commutative, the single data point may be provided in and the data point matrix may be provided in as well.

member.summary: Finds sequential indices of non-zero elements in n-d array, search from start to end in column major order.
member.returns: Sequential indices of the non-zero-valued elements in .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.find(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},System.Int64,System.Boolean,ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Find sequential indices of non-zero elements in n-d array, searches from start to end in column major order.
member.param: [Optional] Search direction backwards. Default: (false) start at the first element and search to the last element of .
[Optional] If non-null on entry: the function returns the row indices and gives column indices in . Default: (null) the function returns the sequential indices of elements found only.
[Optional] Maximum number of non-zero elements to find. Default: (0) find all non-zero elements.
[Optional] Return the found non-zero element values in . Default: (null) don't return the values.
member.returns: Sequential, column major ordered indices of the non-zero-valued elements in or row indices if is not null.

remarks.para: If or are not null on entry they are filled with the requested respective info as column vectors. If is not null it contains the column indices of non-zero values. If has more than two dimensions subsequent dimensions are merged into the second dimension and the indices given in are considered sequential indices of (column major order).
Note, that the array returned by corresponds to the indices of the rows of non-zero values if is not null and to sequential indices of those non-zero values if is null.
Negative values of are considered as abs(n).
If is true starts searching for non-zero values from the last element and proceeds in column major order to the first element or until non-zero elements were found, whatever comes first.
Find() returns and considers indices as 64 bit . Overloads exist for backwards compatibility which expect indices as values. Such functions are decorated with the suffix '32' in their names.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.ind2sub``6(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64},System.Int32)
member.summary: Computes dimensional indices from squential indices.
member.param: The input array providing the size, strides and element type to compute subscript indices for.
Sequential ('linear') indices into . n elements of arbitrary shape.
member.returns: A matrix [m, n], where m = .S.NumberOfElements and n = A.S.NumberOfDimensions. Indices for each dimension are stored in columns.

remarks.para: This function converts sequential element indices into subscript indices. Subscript indices specify the position of an element in by giving the position of the element in each dimension individually. Hence, n subscript indices are required to describe the element position in . In contrast to that, sequential indices specify the position of an element in by a single sequential index, where all elements are considered to be 'lined-up'. The sequential index is than simply the index of the element in the line.
The (virtual) lining-up of the elements in is performed in column major order. Note, that the order considered by is not related to the actual order of the elements as they are stored in memory.
If is not a vector its elements are read in column major order.

If the optional parameter is positive it specifies the number of output subscript dimensions to compute. This number can differ from the actual number of dimensions in . If is smaller than the number of dimensions in unspecified trailing dimensions of are virtually merged and the last column of subscript indices holds the indices into those merged dimension. Note, that in order to use these indices to address elements of subarray indexing must be performed in = .
If is larger than .S.NumberOfDimensions then subscripts in columns corresponding to virtual dimensions of will be '0'.
The matrix returned gives the subscripts for each element index in in rows. The matrix stores m rows of subscripts, corresponding to m elements in .

can contain values addressing non-existing elements in (indices out-of-range). These indices will produce out-of-range subscript indices also. In they may be used to grow the size of an array in a left-side index expression. does not give an error for out-of-range elements nor for negative values in ! The special meaning of latter (i.e.: counting from the end) is not considered here.
and are equivalent operations, inverting the results of the respective other function. Combining both functions creates a roundtrip and gives the original data.

member.exception: if has less than 1 dimension.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.isequal(ILNumerics.BaseArray,ILNumerics.BaseArray)
member.summary: Compares the number, shape, and type of elements of and and returns true if both are the same.
member.returns: True, if all elements and sizes of both arrays match; false otherwise.

remarks.para: Binary comparison is used on the elements. For floating point elements slight round-off errors will cause the comparison to fail! Use 'allall(abs(A - B) < tol)' or similar for floating point arrays instead. The same is recommended when performance is a critical factor: (just like the underlying function ) does not parallelize automatically and is recommended for simple, non-performance critical comparisons only.

If both arrays differ only in singleton dimensions but the types and (binary) values of all corresponding elements are equal the comparison can still succeed. Consider using additionally for a stricter comparisons including singleton dimensions.
This function is an alias for which overrides . In difference to latter the function does not perform reference comparison but the type and value of the elements are compared too.

member.summary: Computes the (flattened, row-major) sequential index and value of the element with the maximum value in .
member.param: Array to compute the maximum for. This is not altered.
[Optional] index of the maximum value. Default: (null) the index is not returned.
[Optional] iteration order for the flattened sequential indices. Default: .
[Optional] determins how NaN values are handled for floating point element types. Ignored for integer elements. Defaul: (true) ignores NaNs.
member.returns: Scalar array with the maximum value in A.

remarks.para: See for getting the maximum values along a specific dimension.

The functions 'max','min','maxall','minall' give all similar results between the framework APIs (ILNumericsV4/Matlab(R) / numpy) but show individual behavior regarding the handling of floating point NaN values and iteration order. The value of 'true' for corresponds to the behavior of ILNumerics version 4/ Matlab(R). Only if all elements in are the value of the result will also be NaN. This is the default.

The value of 'false' for gives the numpy behavior: NaN values take precedence over non-NaN values. If one element in the set of values is NaN the result will also be NaN. This is the default behavior for such functions defined as [numpy API] extension methods on the array classes.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.meshgrid(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Create two matrices for evaluation and visualization of 2 dimensional functions over a 2d grid.
member.param: [Output, Optional]: if on entry is not null it holds the values for the Y dimension on return.
member.returns: X values matrix along the values of . Corresponding values for Y are returned in .

remarks.para: The matrices returned can conveniently be used to evaluate and visualize functions of 2 variables over a grid of (X Y) positions.

Note that the X dimension goes along the rows, while the second dimension is considered the columns! This deviates from the common intuition and the actual storage order of matrix elements (i.e.: first dimension along the columns and 2nd dimension along the rows). The reason for it is the convenience this order gives for plotting purposes: In most plots the X axis is expected to run horizontaly.

member.exception: If or is null.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.meshgrid(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Create 3d arrays for evaluation and visualization of 3 dimensional functions.
member.param: [Output, Optional] If on entry is not null it holds the values for the y dimension on return.
[Output, Optional] If on entry is not null it holds the values for the z dimension on return.

remarks.para: The arrays returned can conveniently be used to evaluate and visualize functions of 3 variables X, Y and Z. Coordinates build a 3 dimensional grid with edges at all permutations of , and .

member.summary: Create reshaped, one dimensional version of . Flattens the array to a vector.
member.param: Length of the vector produced. This must be equal to or a negative number.
[Optional] Storage order for the new array. Default: null ().
member.returns: A new array with the same values as this array, lined up in a 1-dimensional vector.

remarks.para: The (redundant) parameter indicates the number of elements along the first dimension for the returned array. If is positive, its value must equal the number of elements in array . If is negative, the correct number of elements is substituted automatically.
The setting of is taken into account. Therefore - by default - the array returned will have 2 dimensions, since the default value for is 2.
The storage order for both: the order for reading the elements from this array and storing the element into the reshaped array is determined as follows:

list.item: If is specified ( or ) its value is used for the output. A copy is made only if really needed.
Otherwise, the value of determins the target storage order.

remarks.para: A copy of the elements is required for non-continous arrays and - except for vector shaped arrays - for unmatching order settings. Otherwise the returned array references the same memory as this array with a modified size descriptor.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.sub2ind``6(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64})
member.summary: Computes sequential (linear) indices from dimensional indices.
member.param: The input array providing the size, strides and element type to compute the sequential indices for.
Dimensional index tuples into as m elements of n rows. Matrix [m, n].
member.returns: Vector [m] with sequential element indices into according to the subscript indices (rows) from .

remarks.para: This function converts subscript indices into sequential element indices. Subscript indices specify the position of an element in by giving the position of the element in each dimension individually. Hence, n subscript indices are required to describe a single element position in . In contrast to that, sequential indices specify the position of an element in by a single sequential index, where all elements are considered to be 'lined-up'. The sequential index is than simply the index of the element in the line.

The (virtual) lining-up of the elements in is performed in column major order. Note, that the order considered by and by is not related to the actual order of the elements as they are stored in memory.
If has fewer columns as dimensions exist in indices into unspecified dimensions are considered 0. The last column of may contains values as indices into the merged trailing dimensions of .

The vector returned gives the sequential index for each element specified as a row in . A sequential index corresponds to the 0-based index of the element after lining-up all elements of , starting at element 0 and walking along the array in column major order.

can contain values addressing non-existing elements in (indices out-of-range). These indices will produce invalid sequential indices and do not produce an error. Also, no error is generated for negative values in ! The special meaning of latter (i.e.: counting from the end) is not considered here.
and are equivalent operations, inverting the results of the respective other function. Combining both functions creates a roundtrip and gives the original data.

member.exception: if has less than 1 dimension.
if or are null.

member.summary: Sort strings in A along dimension 'dim'
member.param: Input array. A may be an empty, scalar, vector or matrix.
Specifies the direction of sorting: true: descending sort direction; false: ascending
member.returns: Sorted array of the same size/shape as A

remarks.para: The strings in A will be sorted lexicographically in ascending order using the bucket sort algorithm. Data along the first non singleton dimension will get sorted independently from data in the other rows/columns.
The sorting order of strings is determined char-wise by comparing the ASCII codes of the characters.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.sort(ILNumerics.InArray{System.String},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sort data in A along dimension 'dim'
member.param: Input array: empty, scalar, vector or matrix
member.returns: Sorted array of the same size as A

remarks.para: The data in A will be sorted using the bucket sort algorithm. Data along the dimension will get sorted independently from data in the next row/column.
This overload also returns an array 'Indices' which will hold the indices into the original elements after sorting. Elements of 'Indices' are of type double.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.MathInternal.sort``3(ILNumerics.InArray{``0},ILNumerics.OutArray{``2},System.Int32,System.Boolean,ILNumerics.Core.Misc.KeyMapper{``0,``1})
member.summary: Generic bucket sort algorithm in A along arbitrary dimension
member.param: Input array: empty, scalar, vector or matrix
[Input/Output] The values in Indices will be returned in the same sorted order as the elements in A. This can be used to derive a permutation matrix of the sorted indices.
member.typeparam: Element type of values of A
Subelement type. For element type of string this would be 'char'
member.param: Instancce of an object of type ILKeyMapper. This object must be derived from ILKeyMapper{T,SubelementType} and match the generic argument . It will be used to split single elements into its subelements and map their content into bucket numbers. For all reference types except those of type string you will have to write your own ILKeyMapper class for that purpose.
member.returns: Sorted array of the same size as A

remarks.para: The data in A will be sorted using the bucket sort algorithm. Data along the dimension will get sorted independently. I.e., for dim = 0, columns are sorted independently.

This overload also returns an array 'Indices' which will hold the indices into the original elements after sorting. Therefore, the unsorted indices must be provided by the user on entry. Indices must not be null.

This generic version is able to sort arbitrary element types. Even user defined reference types can be sorted by specifying a user defined ILKeyMapper class instance. Also the type of Indices may be arbitrarily choosen. In difference to the regular sort function overload, Indices must manually be given to the function on entry. Elements in 'Indices' are sorted in the same order as the elements of A.

By using this overload you may use the same permutation matrix several times to reflect the manipulations done to A due multiple sort processes. The Indices given will directly be used for the sorting disregarding initial order.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.numpyInternal.max(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the maximum of elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] True: reduced singleton dimension is not removed from the output (default). False: the new singleton dimension is removed.
The index of the dimension to be reduced.
[Optional] Output: 0-based index values of the found elements along the working dimension. Default: (null) don't return the indices.
member.returns: New array with the same shape as except that the dimension specified by is reduced to length min(1,A.S[dim]) and removed if is false.

remarks.para: Empty arrays are handled in the same way as other shapes: the dimension specified by is reduced to 1. If A.S[dim] == 0 the s dimension length in the array returned will also be 0.
Scalar arrays: numpy scalars give a numpy scalar (0 dim) as output.

Special floating point values (for floating point element types): positive and negative infinity are handled in the regular way. NaN ('not a number') values are ignored. If all elements in a working dimension are NaN, NaN is returned as result in the corresponding output element.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If the storage of on entry is sufficient (i.e.: large enough and not shared with other arrays) it will be directly used for storing the indices and I is reshaped as required. Otherwise, a new array is created and returned. In order to safe the index computation null can be provided as which is the default.

If is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined and may point to the first or any other occurrence of the value returned from the working dimension.

member.exception: If A.S[dim] == 0 and was false.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.numpyInternal.put``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},ILNumerics.InArray{``0},ILNumerics.PutModes)
member.summary: Replaces elements of with at positions given by sequential (i.e.: flatten, row-major) .
member.typeparam: Element type of indices. Must be numeric.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be replaced.
Index array. The shape is ignored. Values must be numeric and are read in row-major order.
Values array. The shape is ignored. Values are read in row-major order.
[Optionl] Specifies how to handle index values in which are out-of-range. Default: error.

remarks.para: This function has a similar effect as doing A.flat[indices] = values in numpy. However, in ILNumerics the iterator returned from A.flat is read-only. Use as a replacement.

Note that the values in are considered sequential indices, i.e. they correspond to the element position in a flattened array, where the flattening is performed in row-major order. For performance reasons and if . is not A is converted to row-major storage layout first and remains in row-major storage after the function returns. Note further, that the conversion happens proactively, and is not rolled back in case of errors during the iteration.
Elements of can be negative, which corresponds to indexing from the end of flattened .
Repeated values in lead to only the last corresponding value in to be stored at the respective position in .

If has more elements than are indices provided in superfluent values are ignored. No exception is thrown in this case. If has fewer elements than indices are provided in existing values are repeated as necessary.

The parameter determines what happens with indices laying outside of the bounds of A. The default value of throws an in this case. Two other options exist which bring the index back into the valid range: computes the modulus, limits the indices to the allowed range. Note that negative indices behave as usual (counting from the end of A) for modes and only.
requires the element type of to be value types (struct, commonly numeric).

member.exception: if is and any element in is out of the allowed range of [-A.S.NumberOfElements...>= A.].

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Functions.Builtin.numpyInternal.repeat``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Repeat elements along a flattened array or a specific axis.
member.typeparam: Element type of . Must be an integer type.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be repeated.
[Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) flatten A and repeat all values along dimension #0.

remarks.para: This function repeats elements of along a single dimension. By default, where no is defined is reshaped to a vector in row-major order and all elements are repeated according to . Otherwise, if an was specified, repetitions are performed along that dimension only. In this case, the array returned has the same shape as , except that the working dimension is enlarged.

The shape of is ignored. Its values give the counts for each element along the axis . Values must be numeric, positive integers and are read in row-major order. If has exactly one element all elements along the working dimension of are repeated by the same number. Alternatively, the length of must match A.S[axis] to specify individual repetition counts for each element along the working dimension. Thus, if is null (default) can be a scalar or an array with 'A.S.NumberOfElements == repeats.S.NumberOfElements'.
This function returns a new array and does not alter or any input parameters.

member.exception: if any of the or is null

if points to a virtual dimension; if is not a numeric array, is of a shape which is not broadcastable to the length of the working dimension or contains elements which are not convertible to positive integer values;

summary.para: Base class for memory resources. All types handling memory in various ways derive from . This class either wraps a simple pointer to unmanaged memory or a reference to a managed array of various element types. Instances are subject of garbage collection (as a fallback only), perform reference counting and are happy to be used in a multithreaded consumer / provider scenario.
Typically, is allocated, stored and maintained by a corresponding .

member.summary: An identifier for this memory object.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryHandle.Pointer
member.summary: The memory address of host (unmanaged heap) memory represented by this memory handle.

remarks.para: The pointer returned is only valid on host devices and only as long as the current thread does not enqueue any new asynchronous operations (involving this same memory handle). Typically, you acquire the pointer, immediately perform some (low level) operations on its memory, and - as the program proceeds with new array operations - forget about its value.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryHandle.Retain(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Register a reference to this handle. This method is threadsafe.
member.param: [Optional] Synchronous operations may acquire a write lock based on the number of references currently existing for this buffer. Default: false.

remarks.para: Note that the write lock acquired by is only valid on this (main) thread and only in synchronous operations on buffer / handles. It is solely based on the number of references to this handle and will not prevent asynchronous operations (segments, copies) to access the handle for writing! Such operations rely on other synchronization methods (events). The method will fail if is true but the number of references pointing to this handle is not suited for writing. Expected number of references: 2 (one for hosting array, one for caller operation)

member.exception: if a write lock was requested but could not be acquired.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryHandle.Release
member.summary: Releases one reference to this handle. May causes the handle to be returned to the pool if this is the last reference pointing to the handle. This method is threadsafe.
member.remarks: This method may be called by the base class' finalizer!

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryHandle.Dispose(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Attempt to release this handle, neglecting any ref counting. This method really gives up the unmanaged resources and is called during finalization of CriticalHandle (among others).

remarks.para: is implemented in a way that the first thread executing this method is releasing the underlying resource and marks this handle as invalid. Note, that is called exactly once (by this first thread only). Care must be taken if the resource is managed by reference counting and multiple references exist.
This method is threadsafe.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryPool`1.ShrinkCount
member.summary: Number of shrinking operations performed by the pool so far.

remarks.para: A high number of shrinking operations indicate an suboptimal memory configuration for the current problem size / system memory. In such a situation (at least some) memory chunks are not optimally reused and the performance of the application may be low.
During the run of the algorithm the pool will try to adopt itself to the required memory allocation pattern. This means the pool is shrinked and expanded as required dynamically.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryPool`1.OOMCount
member.summary: Number of OOMs catched (and handled) during allocation requests.

remarks.para: A high number of OOM exceptions caught during the run of the algorithms may indicate insufficient memory on your system for the particular problem size. Try to limit the memory used by other processes and /or threads and to increase the memory available to the thread this pool is associated with.
Try to increase the physical RAM available on your system.
OOM exceptions cause the memory pool to decrease its overall storage limit so that fewer objects are kept alive by the pool.

member.summary: Handle representing unmanaged host memory in a robust (self-disposing) way. Aligned in certain cases.
member.remarks:
The pointer to native memory wrapped inside this handle will be acquired from the unmanaged heap. For performance reason the acquiring class / method is responsible for initializing new handles with required data: Length and Pointer.
In case of will present the lowest address within the allocated memory region which fulfills the alignment and length requirements of Intel's OpenCL buffer sharing (CPU / Integrated GPU). See: which determines the needed alignment (4K). The length of the buffer
Note, that alignment for is only guaranteed for handles pointing to memory regions larger than .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Native.MKLFFT.FreePlans
member.summary: Invalidates the currently cached fft descriptor for this thread.

remarks.para: Calling this method manually may help in situations where multithreading was triggered manually and many threads are involved. Note that FFT plans are cached on a thread level! Therefore, if you have created fft transforms on multiple threads, make sure to dispose the descriptor on each thread individually.

FFT descriptors carry information about the last FFT transform and reuse it for subsequent, similar transforms on the same thread. This saves the re-creation of intermediate data during the transforms. Only the descriptor of the last FFT transform is cached. Hence, in a single threaded scenario (default) disposing the FFT descriptor data manually is rarely required.

member.name: T:ILNumerics.Core.Native.ILapack
member.summary: Interface for LAPACK/BLAS functions.
member.remarks:
Each native module must implement this interface explicitly. Calls to native functions are made by calling functions of this interface. Therefore the user can transparently call any function regardless of the plattform the assymbly (currently) runs on. The native modules implementing this interface take care of the details of implementation.
Usually users of the library will not have to handle with this interface. Its functions will be used from inside built in functions and are therefore wrapped (mainly from inside ILNumerics.ILMath).
Every LAPACK/BLAS function is explicitly implemented for any type supported. e.g. IILLapack includes four functions doing general matrix multiply: dgemm, zgemm, cgemm and sgemm - for all four floating point datatypes supported from the LAPACK package.
LAPACK is an open source linear algebra functions package optimized for use together with highly natively optimized BLAS functions. A LAPACK guide is available here: www.netlib.org.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Native.ILapack.dgesdd(System.Char,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double*,System.Int32,System.Double*,System.Double*,System.Int32,System.Double*,System.Int32,System.Int32@)
member.summary: singular value decomposition, new version, more memory needed
member.param:
Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix U
jobz value ... will result in:
A all M columns of U and all N rows of V**T are returned in the arrays U and VT
S the first min(M,N) columns of U and the first min(M,N) rows of V**T are returned in the arrays U and VT
O If M >= N, the first N columns of U are overwritten on the array A and all rows of V**T are returned in the array VT, otherwise, all columns of U are returned in the array U and the first M rows of V**T are overwritten in the array VT
N no columns of U or rows of V**T are computed.
The number of rows of the input matrix A. M greater or equal to 0.
The number of columns of the input matrix A. N greater or equal to 0

On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit,
if JOBZ = 'O', A is overwritten with the first N columns of U (the left singular vectors, stored columnwise) if M >= N; A is overwritten with the first M rows of V**T (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise) otherwise.
if JOBZ .ne. 'O', the contents of A are destroyed.
The leading dimension of the array A. LDA ge max(1,M).
array, dimension (min(M,N)). The singular values of A, sorted so that S(i) ge S(i+1)
The leading dimension of the array U. LDU >= 1; if JOBZ = 'S' or 'A' or JOBZ = 'O' and M < N, LDU >= M

array, dimension (LDVT,N). If JOBZ = 'A' or JOBZ = 'O' and M >= N, VT contains the N-by-N orthogonal matrix V**T; if JOBZ = 'S', VT contains the first min(M,N) rows of V**T (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise); if JOBZ = 'O' and M < N, or JOBZ = 'N', VT is not referenced

list.item: 0: successful exit.
< 0 : if INFO = -i, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
> 0 : ?BGSDD did not converge, updating process failed.

member.remarks: (From the lapack manual):DGESDD computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a real M-by-N matrix A, optionally computing the left and right singular vectors. If singular vectors are desired, it uses a divide-and-conquer algorithm. The SVD is written A = U * SIGMA * transpose(V) where SIGMA is an M-by-N matrix which is zero except for its min(m,n) diagonal elements, U is an M-by-M orthogonal matrix, and V is an N-by-N orthogonal matrix. The diagonal elements of SIGMA are the singular values of A; they are real and non-negative, and are returned in descending order. The first min(m,n) columns of U and V are the left and right singular vectors of A. Note that the routine returns VT = V**T, not V. The divide and conquer algorithm makes very mild assumptions about floating point arithmetic. It will work on machines with a guard digit in add/subtract, or on those binary machines without guard digits which subtract like the Cray X-MP, Cray Y-MP, Cray C-90, or Cray-2. It could conceivably fail on hexadecimal or decimal machines without guard digits, but we know of none.

member.remarks: (From the lapack manual):DGESDD computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a real M-by-N matrix A, optionally computing the left and right singular vectors. If singular vectors are desired, it uses a divide-and-conquer algorithm. The SVD is written A = U * SIGMA * transpose(V) where SIGMA is an M-by-N matrix which is zero except for its min(m,n) diagonal elements, U is an M-by-M orthogonal matrix, and V is an N-by-N orthogonal matrix. The diagonal elements of SIGMA are the singular values of A; they are real and non-negative, and are returned in descending order. The first min(m,n) columns of U and V are the left and right singular vectors of A. Note that the routine returns VT = V**T, not V. The divide and conquer algorithm makes very mild assumptions about floating point arithmetic. It will work on machines with a guard digit in add/subtract, or on those binary machines without guard digits which subtract like the Cray X-MP, Cray Y-MP, Cray C-90, or Cray-2. It could conceivably fail on hexadecimal or decimal machines without guard digits, but we know of none.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.Native.ILapack.cgesdd(System.Char,System.Int32,System.Int32,ILNumerics.fcomplex*,System.Int32,System.Single*,ILNumerics.fcomplex*,System.Int32,ILNumerics.fcomplex*,System.Int32,System.Int32@)
member.summary: singular value decomposition, new version, more memory needed
member.param:
Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix U
jobz value ... will result in:
A all M columns of U and all N rows of V**T are returned in the arrays U and VT
S the first min(M,N) columns of U and the first min(M,N) rows of V**T are returned in the arrays U and VT
O If M >= N, the first N columns of U are overwritten on the array A and all rows of V**T are returned in the array VT, otherwise, all columns of U are returned in the array U and the first M rows of V**T are overwritten in the array VT
N no columns of U or rows of V**T are computed.
The number of rows of the input matrix A. M greater or equal to 0.
The number of columns of the input matrix A. N greater or equal to 0

On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit,
if JOBZ = 'O', A is overwritten with the first N columns of U (the left singular vectors, stored columnwise) if M >= N; A is overwritten with the first M rows of V**T (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise) otherwise.
if JOBZ .ne. 'O', the contents of A are destroyed.
The leading dimension of the array A. LDA ge max(1,M).
array, dimension (min(M,N)). The singular values of A, sorted so that S(i) ge S(i+1)
The leading dimension of the array U. LDU >= 1; if JOBZ = 'S' or 'A' or JOBZ = 'O' and M < N, LDU >= M

array, dimension (LDVT,N). If JOBZ = 'A' or JOBZ = 'O' and M >= N, VT contains the N-by-N orthogonal matrix V**T; if JOBZ = 'S', VT contains the first min(M,N) rows of V**T (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise); if JOBZ = 'O' and M < N, or JOBZ = 'N', VT is not referenced

list.item: 0: successful exit.
< 0 : if INFO = -i, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
> 0 : ?BGSDD did not converge, updating process failed.

member.name: F:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.SizeOfT
member.summary: Number of bytes used to store a single element of type in memory [readonly].

remarks.para: corresponds to the unmanged size of a single element of this array. This size corresponds to . Its value is cached here for performance reasons.
Note that the size of blittable types is the same on the managed as well as on the unmanaged part. For example, every element of type consumes 4 bytes in the unmanaged heap or on the managed stack.
(At least) one exception exists: elements in .NET are represented by 4 bytes on the managed side. ILNumerics, however, stores them more efficiently as single in memory.

member.remarks: Be cautious when using this property on existing arrays, which have references, either by local array variables or by other means! The return type array may violates the rule for RetT to never be shared with anything. Such return type may only be used on new storages which have not yet exposed to user code. Commonly, their reference count is 0. The ref count of the RetT returned is incremented (1).

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.ScopeState
member.summary: Gets the state of this storage: 0 - outside any scope, 1 - prepared to enter scope, 2 - waiting for leaving a scope & for Release().
member.remarks: THIS IS NOT USED IN VERSION 5 SCOPING. IT IS LEFT IN HERE BECAUSE WE NEED IT FOR VERSION 6 SCOPING ONCE WE HAVE COMPILER SUPPORT. Edit, v.7: time went by so fast ... We don't use it in version 7 either. It is left as TODO. Scope / lifetime of arrays is a static feature and could be optimized by the compiler...! Edit2, v7.0: ok, all back to start. We need the scope flag to support multithreading, but also accelerated code and array renaming. Example: Assume a local array in accelerated code /legacy fallback code / completed awaiter (fft) a.s.o. The local is registered in the current scope (see, f.e.: fftforward1D). Now, the local is renamed, released and marked for not being released again. This would cache the storage and make it accessible for further arrays. However, the storage remains in the current scope! When the scope is left, it checks for the storage being marked for disposal. With a simple 'int' flag we had the chance that the storage was revived in the meantime and the scope flag was back enabled (from another thread or from accelerated code). This would dispose the storage - which is now unrelated - and would be a bug (aka as race condition)! Below change stores the target scope_info_ as a backreference into the storage. In LeaveScope the array is only disposed by the scope (reference identity) stored into m_scopeState. If both do not match the storage is not disposed. Leaving the scope is possible by clearing the flag. Assigning a new storage via Assign simply exchanges both storages from the ScopeInfo in the individual scope, which remains in place untouched. (No need to find and remove the storage in the collection of registered storages! -> O(1)). The only drawback: this does not support multiple threads! Though, it is hard to construct a case where this would be an issue: If a single local array is brougth into a scoped region and accessed by multiple threads ... Note, that the InArray case seems to be not affected, since there are no variables (only function arguments) of InArray type. Such argument is disposed by the caller's scope (where the implicit conversion happens), not by ending the local scope.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.Clone
member.summary: Creates a shallow copy of this storage. Supports pending storages.
member.returns: Shallow, lazy clone of this , having the size of and sharing the memory handles with this storage.

remarks.para: The storage returned has a reference count of 1 and an asynch reference count of 1 (2 when this is a pending storage). The reference count for the (shared) buffer set is increased. The clone owns its own size structure, now exposing the same size information as this storage, including dimensions and strides.
If Clone() was called on a pending storage the cloned storage returned will be pending as well. However, the State objects representing the pending operations may or may not be the same instance.

When the current storage comprises elements of a managed type (non-numerical arrays, as, for example: cell or Array{string}) the clone returned likely comprises of copies of the source elements. This is an unspecified implementation detail.

member.remarks: The hash code is generated by taking the values currently stored in the array into account. Therefore, the function must iterate over all elements in the array - which makes it a somehow expensive operation. Take this into account when considering to use large arrays in collections like dictionaries or hashtables, which make great use of hash codes.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.DetachBufferSetInplace(System.UInt32)
member.summary: Makes sure that this storage uses a dedicated buffer set - not being shared with other storages. This is required but not sufficient for enabling writes to this storage!
member.param: [Optional] The device the current data of this storages device specific memory shall be copied onto. (ONAL: not used)
member.remarks:
This function ensures that...
this storage uses memory which is not shared by other storages. If memory is currently shared, the memorys data is copied to a new memory region which is then current to this storage.
Note that this function does not check whether this storage is shared by multiple arrays (InArray, local array, output arrays). It does neither check if this storage is being used by (other) asynch operations! Both checks must be performed also, in order to prepare a storage for writing!
While during common use and when accessing a local array this local array will be the only array referencing the storage there are situations when other arrays may reference a storage. Examples include the handling of input array types, the use of this storage in asynchronous operations and when local arrays () are defined as attributes of classes. Therefore, it is recommended to ensure that no other arrays currently exist which share this storage: == 1 && == 1.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.GetDetached(System.UInt32)
member.summary: Creates a new, detached (writable) storage. Out of-place! -> Does not change this storage!
member.param: [Optional] the device ID of the target device data must be copied to.
member.returns: The detached storage or this storage.

remarks.para: This version of GetDetached() is used by default since version 7.0. It works 'Out Of-Place' and allows to mutate / exchange this storage atomically, when required. The storage returned points to a new storage or to this storage. Use reference comparison to detect, if a clone was made (a new storage reference) or not (same reference).

Note, this function evolved from and replaces DetachBufferset() in earlier releases. It does no longer mutate this storage directly. Instead, when required a new storage is created (copied) and returned instead. Callers must decide if Assign() is required or not. This allows to use GetDetached() in a chain of mutations (f.e.: SetRangeML())

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.Dispose
member.summary: Expert interface: disposes this array storage. This must be the last action performed on this object! Afterwards, this object can not be used anymore!

remarks.para: During regular use ILNumerics arrays are cleaned up automatically and deterministically. Users should not call explicitly! However, if Dispose was called on an array A, A cannot be used anymore thereafter! Note, that it is even illegal to use _any_ reference to this storage afterwards! Even reassigning to a local array variable can cause an exception after calling Dispose() on the local array variable. Or, even worse: (re-)using an array object after calling Dispose() may causes unexpected side effects on subsequent array operations, because the disposed object may be cached and reused in the meantime!
Don't call Dispose() manually! This interface is provided for compatibility with legacy versions only.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.EnsureStorageOrder(ILNumerics.StorageOrders,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Ensures that elements are layed out in a specific, continous storage order.
member.param: The storage order to be enforced. Must be one of: or .
[Optional] Copy the elements to new memory, no matter if the order is correct already (used by Detach()). Default: false.

[Optional] flag instructing the function to work on this storage directly. False: when required a new storage is created and Assign()-ed to the array(s) of this storage. True: when required the storage order is enforced / configured on this storage and without creating a new storage (not thread safe, applicable for local storages, which are not exposed (yet) to other threads. Default: true (work inplace).

remarks.para: Inplace option: by default, the function ensures the required storage order on this storage (inplace). This works, without renaming the array(s) of this storage, hence, is not thread safe. This method is recommended for enforcing a certain storage order on local (mutable) arrays, and for immutable arrays, like RetT and InT type arrays. Latter shall not be renamed (Assign()-ed) due to their specified immutability. (Note the contradiction with changing theirs size, though!)

The not-inplace option (inplace = false) is for thread safety on any array which is potentially exposed to the public. It creates a new storage with the correct storage order and assignes the new storage to the arrays of this storage. Note, that afterwards, the new storage instance must be used for processing subsequent steps going forward. It can be stored from the return value if this function or fetched from the array layer.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.BaseStorage`6.getCheckIterator(ILNumerics.BaseArray,System.UInt32,System.Int64,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Converts incoming base array index/indices into iterator. Source array is NOT released.

members.member:
These methods are used from the array layer, indexing interface. The return RetT (instead of StorageT from the ***_ACC segment interface). Memory management and the prevention from multiple disposes of incoming dimensional indices is done by only wrapping the mutating parts into a try { } finally {} block and releasing the dims only when entering this block. (Recursive) ellipsis handling is excluded from this block. Before an error is generated / thrown from outside the try-finally block ReleaseDims() is explicitly called.
See also: memory management by an additional parameter 'releaseDims' in GetRange_np_Acc.

Finds the minimum and maximum values among all elements of , optionally ignoring special floating point values.
member.param: [Optional] When true only non-infinity and non-NaN values will be considered as regular values. Default: false.
member.returns: True, if the minimum and maximum values could be computed. False otherwise.

remarks.para: The operation is efficiently performed on all elements of the input in a single run.
The operation is performed in multiple threads, according to the current settings of .
The input is not altered.

The function always succeeds and returns true for non-empty arrays of integer (non-floating point) element types. Overloads for floating point element types: the function succeeds on non-empty arrays which have at least one element other than NaN.

The optional parameter is useful, for example, to determine the minimum and maximum values stored inside this storage in order to find scaling factors and for normalization purposes. Here, and can be ignored since they would be not useful as scaling factors. For the default value ('false') infinity values are considered regular values and contribute to the result.

member.summary: Tests if a cell element is of the given array kind/element type.
member.typeparam: The array element type to probe the cell element for.
member.param: Dimensional indices defining the position of the cell element to be probed.
member.returns: true if the element found at the given position is an array of the given element type , false otherwise.

remarks.para: The method is helpful in order to investigate the contents of a cell array. If you are not sure about the types of elements in the cell, this function can be used to make sure that elements actually are of the expected type before attempting to retrieve them.

In most situations, elements of a cell are stored arrays of a distinct element type. That element type is given to as typeparameter . That means, in order to find out, if the first cell element stores an array of int cell.IsTypeOf<int>(0) is used.
In order to test for cell element type can be or : cell.IsTypeOf<Cell>(0).
In order to test for logical element type must be : cell.IsTypeOf<bool>(0).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.IStorage.Clone
member.summary: Creates a shallow copy of this storage. Supports pending storages.
member.returns: Shallow, lazy clone of this , having the size of and sharing the memory handles with this storage.

remarks.para: The storage returned has a reference count of 1 and an asynch reference count of 1 (2 when this is a pending storage). The reference count for the (shared) buffer set is increased. The clone owns its own size structure, now exposing the same size information as this storage, including dimensions and strides.
If Clone() was called on a pending storage the cloned storage returned will be pending as well. However, the State objects representing the pending operations may or may not be the same instance.

When the current storage comprises elements of a managed type (non-numerical arrays, as, for example: cell or Array{string}) the clone returned likely comprises of copies of the source elements. This is an unspecified implementation detail.

member.name: T:ILNumerics.Core.StorageLayer.Iterators.BoolIndexIterator_ML
member.summary: Specialized iterator for ML logical indexing. Does not work with numpy scalars or empty arrays.

remarks.para: This iterator takes an n-dim logical index array and iterates over the sequential indices of its true elements in column major order. No support for numeric index arrays. No support for shared index arrays in the same index space set.

This class is derived from MultidimIterators_np (implementation wise). It is NOT a struct since it will always be used boxed into an IIndexIterator interface (ML style subarray expressions involving Logical arrays -> see: GetRange_ML / SetRange_ML). The iterator is capable of iterating over the bool storage without a consolidating index array for the element positions of the true elements. It performs best for small bool indides and when the bool index does not need to be iterated over multiple times.
No checks are made for the length of dimensions / indices being within an allowed range etc. All checks must be made by the user of the class.

Implementation notes: Similarly to MultidimIterator_np this logical iterator DOES NOT accept numpy scalars (0 dim) bool arrays. This should naturally happen rarely: such scalars are created in numpy ArrayStyle only. However, we are working around this as follows: numpy scalars are presented as 1D arrays by providing strides and dims pointer which point to the '1' describing "Number of Elements" in the original BSD[1] element. The m_nrDims attribute of this iterator is set to 1 than and the original strides and dims pointer from the arrays BSD can be reused in the iterator. Hence, the iterator really ever sees arrays with 1D or more.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.InArray`1.op_Implicit(System.Array)~ILNumerics.InArray{`0}
member.summary: Implicitly convert n-dimensional System.Array to ILNumerics array.
member.returns: If A is null: empty array. Otherwise a new ILNumerics array of the same size as A.
member.exception: If the type of the elements in A cannot get converted to .
If the type of the elements in A is not supported.

remarks.para: Elements of A will be copied to elements of the output array (shallow copy). The following element types are supported for and : double, float, int, uint, long, ulong, short, ushort, sbyte, byte.
Alternatively, may consists out of scalar Arrays (or RetArray, InArray, OutArray) of one of the above element types.

The resulting Array will reflect all dimensions of A. Due to the fact that .NET System.Arrays are stored in row major order and ILNumerics stores array in column major (for compatibility with e.g. Matlab and Fortran) the resulting Array will have its dimensions reverted! For matrices this corresponds to a matrix transpose.

System.Convert is used for the conversion of elements in A to destination elements. This includes widening and narrowing conversions. When, for example, array elements of type double are provided and is Int32 the conversion will round the source elements. See the examples below.

example.code:
'' Elements of System.Value types: Dim A1 As Array(Of Double) = { 1, 2, 3 } ' provide int elements Dim A2 As Array(Of Double) = { 1.0, 2.9, 3.4, 5.12 } ' provide double elements Dim A As Double = 5 Dim B As Double = 6 Dim C As Double = 7
Dim A3 As Array(Of Double) = { A, B, C } ' provide double variables
Dim A4 As Array(Of Double) = { ILMath.cos(A), ILMath.tan(B) * C, C, 3 } ' provide mixed element types, including scalar Array

member.name: M:ILNumerics.InArray`1.AsReadOnlySpan(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.StorageOrders})
member.summary: Returns a span providing access to this array's internal storage for reading.
member.param: [Optional] The order of elements returned. If order is null (default) the current value of is assumed, which depends on .
member.returns: A span with the exact length needed to hold all elements of this array, referencing the elements of this array, and having the same lifetime as this array.

remarks.para: Depending on the current internal storage layout this array is reordered internally as required before returning the span representing the elements in the requested storage order.

Note, that for returning an array as span it must be ensured that the arrays elements are layed-out continously in memory. Thus, the requested storage order is enforced in advance. This may or may not involve an internal copy of the elements of this array and a (transparent to the user) modification in its storage layout.
The Span returned is only valid as long as this array is alive and before a subsequent modification is performed to this array.

member.summary: Assign another array to this array variable. This is an optional, yet more efficient alternative to using '=' for assigning to the array directly.
member.remarks: By using this method, the storage of this array is immediately released to the memory pool and replaced by the new arrays content. member.name: M:ILNumerics.Globals.BorrowPointer``1(System.IntPtr,System.Int64)
member.summary: Creates a 1D vector by using the pre-allocated memory referenced by .
member.param: Pointer to the memory region to be used as storage for the new 1d ILNumerics . The memory region must be large enough to fit at least as many elements of type into, as is specified by .
The number of elements for the new vector.
member.returns: Vector of given length using the memory region according to as storage.
member.remarks:
As the name suggests the pointer is 'borrowed'! The array returned may be used, without restriction, for creating subarrays, as argument in function invocations, as right side in assignments and so on. However, once all arrays referencing the internal storage based on are released and the memory is no longer needed, it will not be deallocated or otherwise freed! Nor will the memory be hold on by means of any ILNumerics memory pool! Instead, the memory ownership remains with you - the caller of this method.
In order to determine, whether or not all references to the memory have been released use .

member.name: P:ILNumerics.ILMath.FFTImplementation
member.summary: Get or set the currently active implementation for performing fft functions. Default: (if available at runtime), otherwise.
member.remarks: By default, ILNumerics uses the managed fft on all platforms. Only when available (Windows, x64 and with ILNumerics.Core.Native package added) optimized, native MKL implementation is used. In order to enforce using the managed lapack implementation or to provide your own IFFT implementation one can now set this value manually. ILMath.FFTImplementation = new ILNumerics.F2NET.ManagedFFTPACK5()

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.fft(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Fast fourier transform along a specific dimension.
member.param: [Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) first non-singleton dimension of or dimension #0.
member.returns: Complex array of the same size than .

remarks.para: The output array returned will be complex hermitian. I.e. the real part being even and the imaginary part being odd symmetrical.

The forward fourier transform and the inverse fourier transform of a given data array A are mathematically equivalent. It's only a scaling factor which is needed to make sure, A equals ifft(fft(A)). That scaling is introduced in the inverse transform.

The transformation is computed by use of the fully managed translation of FFTPACK Fortran codes (version 5, adopted for multiple precision). Alternatively and on Windows/x64, one may utilize a native, optimized version library by referencing the ILNumerics.Core.Native nuget package. The actual implementation used is automatically selected at ILNumerics startup and accessed via the static member ILMath.FFT. See the online documentation for more details in how to tune/configure and select dedicated native libraries.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.ifftsym(ILNumerics.InArray{ILNumerics.complex},System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Inverse fast fourier transform from complex hermitian input to real data.

member.summary: Inverse fast fourier transform (n-D, complex hermitian, specific size)
member.param: Transformation lengths, specifies the length of the dimensions for the transformation array. The length of dims must be > or equal to the number of dimensions of A. For elements in dim being smaller than corresponding dimension length in A, the dimensions will be truncated, otherwise zeros will be padded.
member.returns: Transformation result, real array of the size specified by the 'dims' parameter

remarks.para: The n-dimensional transformation is computed for the n-dimensional array A. Before the transform, the input is resized according to the 'dims' parameter. Dimensions larger than corresponding entries in 'dim' are truncated, dimensions smaller than corresponding entries in 'dim' are zero padded.

The n-dimensional transformation is equivalent to repeatedly (inplace) computing one dimensional transformations along all dimensions of A. However, using this function may be of magnitudes faster than using 1D transformations. This depends on the algorithm and API provided by the underlying native library.
Since a transform of complex hermitian input data results in the output having the imaginary part equals zero, only the real part is returned for convenience reasons.
No check is made for A being hermitian! If A is not hermitian (by means of round-off errors), the result will be wrong!

The forward fourier transform and the inverse fourier transform of a given data array A are mathematically equivalent. It's only a scaling factor which is needed to make sure, A equals ifft(fft(A)). That scaling is introduced in the inverse transform.

The transformation is computed by use of the fully managed translation of FFTPACK Fortran codes (version 5, adopted for multiple precision). Alternatively and on Windows/x64, one may utilize a native, optimized version library by referencing the ILNumerics.Core.Native nuget package. The actual implementation used is automatically selected at ILNumerics startup and accessed via the static member ILMath.FFT. See the online documentation for more details in how to tune/configure and select dedicated native libraries.

member.exception: is thrown if the dim parameter is null, its length is less then the number of dimensions of A or any element of dims is non-negative

Alternatively and on Windows/x64, one may utilize a native, optimized version library by referencing the ILNumerics.Core.Native nuget package. The actual implementation used is automatically selected at ILNumerics startup and accessed via the static member ILMath.FFT. See the online documentation for more details in how to tune/configure and select dedicated native libraries.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.chol(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Cholesky factorization of a symmetric, positive definite matrix.
member.param: Input matrix. must be a symmetric/hermitian matrix.
Throws an if is found to be not positive definite.
member.returns: Cholesky factorization of .

remarks.para: No check is performed on 's symmetry for performance reasons.
If is true and is found to be not positive definite an is thrown and the operation is canceled.

If is false, check the return value's dimension to determine the success of the operation (unless you are sure, was positive definite). If was found not to be positive definite the matrix returned will be of dimension [k x k] and the result of the cholesky factorization of A[0:k-1;0:k-1]. Here k is the first leading minor of at which was found to be not positive definite.
The factorization is carried out by use of the LAPACK functions DPOTRF, ZPOTRF, SPOTRF or CPOTRF respectively.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.cross(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Boolean,System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Computes the cross product along a dimension of two arrays.
member.param: [Optional] If true: normalize resulting vectors to length 1.0. Default: false.
[Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) the first dimension of length 3.
member.returns: Array with cross products of vectors from and .

remarks.para: and are expected to store the vectors inside the same respective dimensions. This dimension must be of length 3 or longer. If is not specified the working dimension is found by searching for the first dimension of length 3, starting with dimension #0. If no dimension of length 3 is found, uses the first dimension which has more than 3 elements. If no such dimension is found an exception is thrown.
The argument allows to explicitly determine the index of the working dimension. The length of this dimension must be equal to or larger than 3. Both, and must be of the same size.
Elements in the working dimension with indices > #2 are ignored. Corresponding elements in the output array become 0.

member.exception: If the size of and is not the same or if either of or is null, if the working dimension could not be determined or if the determined workign dimension is not at least of length 3.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.det(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Determinant of square matrix.
member.returns: Determinant of .

remarks.para: The determinant is computed by decomposing into upper and lower triangular part using LU decomposition.
The determinant of a scalar matrix is the scalar itself. If is empty an empty array will be returned.

member.example: Creating a nonsingular 4x4 (double) matrix and it's determinant Array<double> A = ILMath.counter<double>(1.0, 1.0, 4, 4); A[1, 0] = 0.0; // ensure that A A[2, 3] = 0.0; // has full rank A <Double> [4,4] 1...16 order:| 1 5 9 13 0 6 10 14 3 7 11 0 4 8 12 16 det(A) //D <Double> [1,1] -360 order:|
member.exception: if is not a square matrix.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.diag``1(ILNumerics.BaseArray{``0},System.Int32)
member.summary: Diagonal matrix or diagonal from matrix.
member.param: [Optional] Index of diagonal to extract/ to create. Default: 0.
member.returns: Depending on the shape of a matrix or a vector with the elements on the specified diagonal of .
member.remarks:
The type of the Array returned will be the same as the type of .
If is a matrix, diag() returns the elements on the 's diagonal as column vector.
If is vector, a square matrix of size [.Length - abs(), .Length - abs()] will be created, having the elements of the 's diagonal of .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.eigGen(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.GenEigenType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors (optional) of symmetric/hermitian inputs and : A*V=lamda*B*V.
member.param: Square, symmetric/hermitian input matrix, size [n x n].
Square, symmetric/hermitian and positive definite matrix, size [n x n].
[Output, optional] Returns the eigenvectors in columns (size [n x n]). Default: (null) eigenvectors are not returned.
[Optional] Determines the eigen problem type. Default: (null) Ax_eq_lambBx: A*V = r*B*V.
[Optional] true: skip tests for and being hermitian. Default: false.
member.returns: Vector [n] of eigenvalues or a diagonal matrix [n,n] with the eigenvalues on the main diagonal if is not null.

remarks.para: This function solves the generalized eigenproblem A*V=lamda*B*V or the problem as specified by .
Eigenvectors in are not normalized! See details about the normalization performed by the underlying Lapack routines.

Internally, the generalized eigenproblem A*V = r*B*V will be reduced to B-1*A*V = r*V using cholesky factorization. The computations are handled by LAPACK functions DSYGV,SSYGV,CHEGV and ZHEGV respectively.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.linsolve(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Solves a system of linear equations, B = A x.
member.returns: Solution x solving the equation multiply(A, x) = B. Size [q, m].

remarks.para:
Depending on the structure and properties of the equation system is solved with different approaches:
If is square (q == n) and an upper or lower triangular matrix, the system is solved via backward- or forward substitution and the LAPACK function ?trtrs. Array<double> A = randn<double>(4,4); // construct 4 x 4 matrix Array<double> B = vector<double>(1.0,2.0,3.0); Array<double> x = linsolve(A,B);
if is square, symmetric /hermitian and positive definite is decomposed into a triangular equation system using cholesky factorization and solved via back-/ forward substitution.
otherwise, if is only square it will be decomposed into upper and lower triangular matrices using LU decomposition and the system than solved with the result.
otherwise, if is [n, q] with q != n, the system is solved using decomposition. Note that can be rank deficient.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.linsolve(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.MatrixProperties@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Solves a system of linear equations, B = Ax, taking hints for the best algorithm.
member.param: [Input, Output] Known / determined matrix properties of .
[Optional] Throws an if was found to be singular or a specific property in could not be confirmed. Default: true.
member.returns: Solution x solving the equation multiply(A, x) = B. Size [q, m].

remarks.para:
If no specific properties of are given in and depending on the actual structure and properties of the equation system is solved with different approaches:
If is square (q == n) and an upper or lower triangular matrix, the system is solved via backward- or forward substitution and the LAPACK function ?trtrs. Array<double> A = randn<double>(4,4); // construct 4 x 4 matrix Array<double> B = vector<double>(1.0,2.0,3.0); Array<double> x = linsolve(A,B);
if is square, symmetric /hermitian and positive definite is decomposed into a triangular equation system using cholesky factorization and solved via back-/ forward substitution.
otherwise, if is only square it will be decomposed into upper and lower triangular matrices using LU decomposition and the system is than solved with the triangular result.
otherwise, if ' is [n, q] with q != n, the system is solved using decomposition. Note that can be rank deficient.

Specifying known properties of in may saves some time in determining these properties. If, for example, is known to be positive definite, providing allows the algorithm to perform cholesky factorization with . However, determines advantageous properties automatically if required.

After returning the structure can be inspected fo the matrix properties of found during the computations. Any bits changed in by the function reflect the path taken within . However, does not determine all properties of automatically. If, let's say: is found to be singular, the function returns (or throws an exception) without determining further properties of A. In order to query specific properties of other functionality may be more appropriate.

If is false inspecting the structure on return is required to verify that a valid solution has been computed. If was found to be singular and is false then will have the flag set. If the computation was performed by QR decomposition for a non-square matrix then the flag may be set.

The internal storage order of and/or may be silently changed by this function. The reason is that most functionality is performed in native LAPACK routines which require a certain storage layout (mostly ). Be prepared that both arrays may point to different memory regions for element storage afterwards! This does not, however, affect the handling of the array with common high level functionality (subarrays, element access etc.).

member.summary: Solve system of linear equations A*x = B, with being a square, upper triangular matrix.
member.param: Input matrix. Size [n,n]. Upper triangular. No check is made for that!
[Output] This value gives the row of , where a singularity has been detected (if any). If is not singular, this will return a negative value.

remarks.para: The solution is determined via backward substitution by using a native LAPACK module.
