member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.lu(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: LU matrix decomposition. Decompose general matrix into strictly upper part and lower part.
member.returns: Triangular matrices L and U composed into a single matrix as returned from LAPACK function ?getrf. Size [m x n].

remarks.para: The matrix returned is composed out of the lower triangular matrix L with unit diagonal and the strictly upper triangular matrix U.
This overload is mostly needed for further operations via Lapack libraries. If you need the L and U matrices directly, consider using the overload instead.
lu uses the Lapack function ?getrf, which is provided by a native LAPACK implementation (mostly Intel's MKL).

member.exception: if input A is not a matrix.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.lu(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Decompose matrix into uper and lower triangular matrices. Also generates pivoting permutation matrix.
member.param: [Output] Upper triangular matrix. Size [min(m,n) x n]. This can be null.
[Output, optional] Permutation matrix . Size [m x m]. Default: (null) do not compute the permutation matrix. L is ordered propery before the function returns.
member.returns: Lower triangular matrix L. Size [m x min(m,n)].

remarks.para: is decomposed into L and so that the equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(P,A) holds within the range of round off errors.

The matrix L returned is a lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal. Depending on the rows of L may be reordered due to pivoting during the triangulation. If is not null on entry (i.e.: the permutation matrix is computed and returned from ) L is truely lower triangular. In this case the equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(P,A) holds. Note, that the result of matrix multiplying L with yields a version of having its rows reordered. permutes the rows of accordingly. Note further, that is suitable to be multiplied to , while some other systems return -1 for reordering the result L** instead.

If is null on entry (i.e.: the permutation matrix is not requested and thus not returned) any permutation performed in the triangulation is reversed before returning L so that the matrix L returned is not guranteed to be lower triangular. Instead, the rows of L are reordered by P-1**L. In this case the simplified equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(A) holds (default).
is a strictly upper triangular matrix. Any permutation is performed on L and not on . Thus, the order of rows of does not depend on .
remarks.example: // Construct a matrix A: Array A = new double[,]{ {1, 2, 3}, {4, 4, 4}, {5, 6, 7} }; // A // [3x3] order: - //(:,:) // 1 2 3 // 4 4 4 // 5 6 7 // // define arrays serving as output arrays for U and P Array U = 1, P = 1; Array L = ILMath.lu(A, U, P); // L // [3,3] 1...1 order:| // 1 0 0 // 0,800000 1 0 // 0,200000 -1,000000 1 // // U // [3,3] 5...1,11022302462516E-15 order:| // 5 6 7 // 0 -0,800000 -1,600000 // 0 0 0,000000 // //P // [3,3] 0...0 order:| // 0 0 1 // 0 1 0 // 1 0 0 L and U are triangular matrices. P is returned as well. The result of L**U gives: multiply(L,U) 5 6 7 4 4 4 1 2 3 This result matches a reordered version of A, which can be computed by help of P: multiply(P,A) 5 6 7 4 4 4 1 2 3
remarks.para: lu uses the Lapack function ?getrf.
The input matrix is not altered.

Either of and/or can be null on entry. If is null the upper triangular matrix will be computed but not returned. Instead, the compressed form of L and is returned as created by the LAPACK function ?getrf:
If is null on entry and is not null the permutation matrix is not computed but rows of L are reordered accordingly in order to fullfill the equation 'A = L**U'.

member.exception: if input is not a matrix.

remarks.para: The matrix returned is composed out of the lower triangular matrix L with unit diagonal and the strictly upper triangular matrix U.
This overload is mostly needed for further operations via Lapack libraries. If you need the L and U matrices directly, consider using the overload instead.
lu uses the Lapack function ?getrf, which is provided by a native LAPACK implementation (mostly Intel's MKL).

member.exception: if input A is not a matrix.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.lu(ILNumerics.InArray{ILNumerics.complex},ILNumerics.OutArray{ILNumerics.complex},ILNumerics.OutArray{ILNumerics.complex})
member.summary: Decompose matrix into uper and lower triangular matrices. Also generates pivoting permutation matrix.
member.param: [Output] Upper triangular matrix. Size [min(m,n) x n]. This can be null.
[Output, optional] Permutation matrix . Size [m x m]. Default: (null) do not compute the permutation matrix. L is ordered propery before the function returns.
member.returns: Lower triangular matrix L. Size [m x min(m,n)].

remarks.para: is decomposed into L and so that the equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(P,A) holds within the range of round off errors.

The matrix L returned is a lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal. Depending on the rows of L may be reordered due to pivoting during the triangulation. If is not null on entry (i.e.: the permutation matrix is computed and returned from ) L is truely lower triangular. In this case the equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(P,A) holds. Note, that the result of matrix multiplying L with yields a version of having its rows reordered. permutes the rows of accordingly. Note further, that is suitable to be multiplied to , while some other systems return -1 for reordering the result L** instead.

If is null on entry (i.e.: the permutation matrix is not requested and thus not returned) any permutation performed in the triangulation is reversed before returning L so that the matrix L returned is not guranteed to be lower triangular. Instead, the rows of L are reordered by P-1**L. In this case the simplified equation ILMath.multiply(L,U) == ILMath.multiply(A) holds (default).
is a strictly upper triangular matrix. Any permutation is performed on L and not on . Thus, the order of rows of does not depend on .
remarks.example: // Construct a matrix A: Array A = new complex[,]{ {1, 2, 3}, {4, 4, 4}, {5, 6, 7} }; // A // [3x3] order: - //(:,:) // 1 2 3 // 4 4 4 // 5 6 7 // // define arrays serving as output arrays for U and P Array U = 1, P = 1; Array L = ILMath.lu(A, U, P); // L // [3,3] 1...1 order:| // 1 0 0 // 0,800000 1 0 // 0,200000 -1,000000 1 // // U // [3,3] 5...1,11022302462516E-15 order:| // 5 6 7 // 0 -0,800000 -1,600000 // 0 0 0,000000 // //P // [3,3] 0...0 order:| // 0 0 1 // 0 1 0 // 1 0 0 L and U are triangular matrices. P is returned as well. The result of L**U gives: multiply(L,U) 5 6 7 4 4 4 1 2 3 This result matches a reordered version of A, which can be computed by help of P: multiply(P,A) 5 6 7 4 4 4 1 2 3
remarks.para: lu uses the Lapack function ?getrf.
The input matrix is not altered.

Either of and/or can be null on entry. If is null the upper triangular matrix will be computed but not returned. Instead, the compressed form of L and is returned as created by the LAPACK function ?getrf:
If is null on entry and is not null the permutation matrix is not computed but rows of L are reordered accordingly in order to fullfill the equation 'A = L**U'.

member.exception: if input is not a matrix.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.norm(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Double)
member.summary: Vector or matrix norm.
member.returns: Array of same type as input array .
member.remarks:
For vectors, must be one of:
0 : returns sqrt(sum(A * A))
System.double.PositiveInfinity: returns max(abs(A))
System.double.NegativeInfinity: returns min(abs(A))
other double values: returns sum(pow(abs(A),degree))^(1/degree)
For matrices must be one of:
0: returns Frobenius norm: sqrt(sum(diag(multiply(A, A.T))))
1: returns 1-norm, max(sum(abs(A)))
2: returns the largest singular value of A, max(svd(A))
PositiveInfinity: returns maxall(sum(abs(A), 1)), the largest value of the sums along the rows
norm(A,0) with A being a vector extends naturally to the frobenius norm for matrices.
For empty arrays A, scalar 0 is returned.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.pinv(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Nullable{System.Double})
member.summary: Moore-Penrose pseudo inverse of .
member.param: [Optional] Tolerance. Default: (null) - use default tolerance (see remarks).
member.returns: Pseudo inverse of input matrix
member.remarks:
The function returns the pseudo inverse (Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse) of input matrix . The return value will be of the same size as .T. It will satisfy the following conditions:
* pinv() * =
pinv() * * pinv() = pinv()
pinv() * is hermitian.
* pinv() is hermitian.
relies on , utilizing native Lapack functions internally. Singular values less than will be set to zero. As default tolerance the following equation is used: \\ tolerance = length() * norm() * eps, where
length() - the longest dimension of .
norm() being the largest singular value of .
eps - the smallest number greater than one.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.qr(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: QR decomposition - raw output as returned from LAPACK.
member.returns: Orthonormal / unitary matrix Q and upper triangular matrix R packed into a single matrix. This is the output of the lapack function ?geqrf.

remarks.para: Input matrix is not altered.

The matrix returned is the direct output of the lapack function [d,s,c,z]geqrf, respectively. It contains the decomposition factors Q and R, but they are combined into a single matrix. Overloads exist which return Q and R individually: .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.qr(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},System.Boolean)
member.summary: QR decomposition, returning Q and , optionally economical sized.
member.param: [Output, optional] Upper triangular matrix . Size [m x n]. Default: (null) same as .
[Optional] True: if m >= n the size of Q and is reduced to [m x m] and [m x n] respectively. Default: false.
member.returns: Orthonormal real / unitary complex matrix Q as result of decomposing . Size [m x m] or [m x min(m,n)] if is true or if A is empty.

remarks.para: The function returns Q and R such that the equation A = Q ** R holds within the range of roundoff errors. ('**' denotes matrix multiplication.)

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.qr(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: QR decomposition with pivoting, potentially size saving shapes.
member.param: [Output, optional] Upper triangular matrix. Size [m x n] or [min(m,n) x n] depending on (see remarks). Default: (null) do not compute .
[Optional] True: return more efficient structures if possible. See remarks for details. Default: false.
[Output, optional] Permutation matrix from pivoting. Size [m x m]. Default: (null) do not return..
member.returns: Orthonormal / unitary matrix Q as result of decomposing . Size [m x m] or [m x min(m,n)], depending on (see remarks).

remarks.para: This function performs the QR decomposition on matrix . It computes matrices Q, and , with Q ** R = A ** E, where '**' denotes matrix multiplication.
If is null on entry, the function returns the compact QR decomposition result from .
If is false, the function returns Q, and such that the equation A * E = Q * R holds within roundoff errors.

If is true ...
and m >= n the size of Q and will be [m x min(m,n)] and [min(m,n) x n] respectively. For m < n the sizes are not changed and as specified above.
the output parameter is returned as vector [n] with permutation indices rather than as a permutation matrix [n,n]. In this case the equation A[":",E] == Q * R holds, except roundoff errors.

reflects the pivoting of done inside the LAPACK function performing the decomposition so that shows increasing diagonal element values. If is not requested (null) the equation Q ** R = A holds instead.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.rank(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},System.Double)
member.summary: Rank of matrix :
member.param: [Optional] Threshold below which a singular value is considered zero. Default: (-1) auto.
member.returns: Rank of matrix .
member.remarks:
The rank is the number of singular values greater than tolerance. If tolerance is smaller than 0 (default), the following default value is used: tol = length(A) * norm(A) * eps, with
length(A) - the longest dimension of
norm(A) - the largest singular value of , see: ,
eps - the distance between 1 and the smallest next greater value.
member.exception: if has more than 2 dimensions.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.all(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Boolean},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Determines whether all elements of along the given dimension are true.
member.param: [Optional] The index of the dimension to be reduced. Default: (-1) the first non-singleton dimension found in or 0.
[Optional] True: reduced singleton dimension is not removed from the output (default). False: the new singleton dimension is removed.
member.returns: New array with the same shape as except that the dimension specified by is reduced to length 1.

remarks.para: For floating point elements: special floating point values (, , etc.; being 'not zero') evaluate to 'true'.
Empty arrays are allowed. In difference to or dimension may be of length 0, which leads to a singleton dimension in the result and the non-existing elements evaluate to 'false'.

The default value for is -1. It causes the function to determine the working dimension (numpy: 'axis') automatically. This search is based on and starts looking at the first dimension for . For , however, the search starts with the last dimension and works its way up to the first dimension. If the array does not contain any non-singleton dimension 0 is returned in both cases.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.and(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'And' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.apply(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},System.Func{System.Double,System.Double,System.Double})
member.summary: Binary, elementwise, broadcasting operation: apply(A,B).
member.param: The elementary (scalar) function to be used to perform the operation on corresponding elements of and .
member.returns: Result of operating elements of and elementwise.

remarks.para: Overloads of expect two arrays of broadcastable size with the same element types. They perform a mapping operation on corresponding elements of and by evaluating for each element of the resulting array.
Overloads of perform fastest where the element type of the input and the output arrays match. Such overloads exist for all numeric value-typed element types.
The function is efficiently parallelized and is evaluated from multiple threads. Make sure that is threadsafe!
For more flexibility a generic overload exist which allows the element types of , as well as the array returned to be individual different. See: .

member.summary: Binary, elementwise, broadcasting apply<T1,T2,long,Tout>(A,B). Maps a scalar operation from elements of and to a third array, provides element index. Arbitrary types. Parallelized.
member.param: The elementary (scalar) function to be used to perform the operation on corresponding elements of and , utilizing respective element values and the index used to locate the output array in iteration order.
member.returns: New or reused array with result of operating elements of and elementwise.

remarks.para: The iteration order depends on the order of input arrays: for column major input i will run in column major order and in row major order for row major inputs. If inputs have other, undefined or different storage orders the result is undefined. It is recommended to use this function on vector input(s) or with a well defined storage order for inputs and/or .
This function may automatically work inplace on either of both input parameters, if possible.

example.para: 'Merge' elements a of an vector of 0's with a scalar -1, weighting with the location index i by applying the function: c = a + i * b.
Efficiently overwrite/initialize the content of an uninitialized array with upwards counting values, row major storage order.

The last example produces the same result as the expression: counter(4,3,2, StorageOrders.RowMajor);. The larger flexibility in the generator function comes with a slight computational overhead, though.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.cell(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{ILNumerics.BaseArray},ILNumerics.StorageOrders)
member.summary: Creates new cell, initialize size and provide arrays for cell elements.
member.param: [Optional] Size hint for the new cell array. Default: (null) Derive the size from .
[Optional] Enumerable of arrays for the cell elements, column major order. Default: (null) creates cell with all 'null' elements.
[Optional] Storage order for the new cell. Default: .
member.returns: Cell of specified size, initialized with given arrays.

remarks.para: If number of arrays given is smaller than the number of elements given by then trailing elements in the cell returned are set to null.
If is null a cell vector is produced with a length corresponding to the number of elements in . Performance wise it is recommended to specify the explicitly, though.
If contains more elements than expected by an error is generated.
The function or one of its overloads are convenient for the specification of dimensional size arguments.
Visit the online documentation for cell.

Note that when is an ILNumerics array (as in the example where was created by the function) memory management is performed accordingly: arrays stored in the object are released and the associated memory is released to the pool after the function returns. However, for of other (non-ILNumerics) types proper memory management is not guaranteed. For example, when providing the target cell element values in a of a copy of individual elements is made by the function before storing the new element into the cell object. The source object remains an element of the system array and is not released!

Therefore, in situations where performance is critical and inside loops use one of the ILNumerics array intialization functions for providing the argument. Otherwise, temporary objects in the may remain live and are left for the GC to clean up (which is fine, except for high performance demands).

member.example: Array A = rand(10,20,30); Cell C = cell(size(3,2),vector(A, A+1, zeros(2,3), "4th element")); //Alternatives: //Cell C = cell(size(3,2),new [] { A, A+1, zeros(2,3) }); //Cell C = cell(size(3,2),row(A, A+1, zeros(2,3))); C >Cell [3,2] > [0]: > [1]: { [10,20,30]} { [1,1]} > [2]: { [10,20,30]} {null} > [3]: { [2,3]} {null}
member.exception: if is not null and the number of elements found in exceeds the expected number of elements as specified by .

remarks.para: The function and the corresponding overloads for providing individual dimension length parameters ,... create n-dimensional numeric arrays with automatically generated values based on a given value and a value. The size of the new array is determined by the parameter(s). The firsts element value is assigned the value. Subsequent values are computed by adding the value of to each elements predecessor.

The term 'predecessor' here means: the predecessor E0 of element E1 is the element having an index I(E0) of I(E1) - 1, where the index I() corresponds to the storage location of the element in memory, relative to the first element.

The storage order is determined by . By default, elements are lined up in memory in column major storage order. must be one out of or . Note, how the storage order affects the order of values in the new array.

example.para: Creating a new array of size [4,3], filled with upwards counting values, starting at 1.

remarks.para: The function and the corresponding overloads for providing individual dimension length parameters ,... create n-dimensional numeric arrays with automatically generated values based on a given value and a value. member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.distL1(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Pairwise L1 distance. Aka: Manhattan distance.
member.returns: pairwise L1 distances between the data point provided in the input vector and the data points stored in the matrix .

remarks.para: If is a colum vector, the distances between and the columns of are calculated. The number of rows of must match the length of vector than. Therefore, the length of the returned vector of distances matches the number of columns of : A.S[1].

If is a row vector, the distances between and the rows of are calculated. The number of columns of must match the length of vector than. Therefore, the length of the returned vector of distances matches the number of rows of : A.S[0].
This function is commutative, the single data point may be provided in and the data point matrix may be provided in as well.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.eq(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Elementwise 'EqualTo' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.find(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},System.Int64,System.Boolean,ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Find sequential indices of non-zero elements in n-d array, searches from start to end in column major order.
member.param: [Optional] Search direction backwards. Default: (false) start at the first element and search to the last element of .
[Optional] If non-null on entry: the function returns the row indices and gives column indices in . Default: (null) the function returns the sequential indices of elements found only.
[Optional] Maximum number of non-zero elements to find. Default: (0) find all non-zero elements.
[Optional] Return the found non-zero element values in . Default: (null) don't return the values.
member.returns: Sequential, column major ordered indices of the non-zero-valued elements in or row indices if is not null.

remarks.para: If or are not null on entry they are filled with the requested respective info as column vectors. If is not null it contains the column indices of non-zero values. If has more than two dimensions subsequent dimensions are merged into the second dimension and the indices given in are considered sequential indices of (column major order).
Note, that the array returned by corresponds to the indices of the rows of non-zero values if is not null and to sequential indices of those non-zero values if is null.
Negative values of are considered as abs(n).
If is true starts searching for non-zero values from the last element and proceeds in column major order to the first element or until non-zero elements were found, whatever comes first.
Find() returns and considers indices as 64 bit . Overloads exist for backwards compatibility which expect indices as values. Such functions are decorated with the suffix '32' in their names.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.flip(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Int32},System.Int32)
member.summary: Flips elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] Index of the working dimension or -1 for determining the working dimension automatically (default).
member.returns: New array with the same shape as .

remarks.para: The working dimension for = -1 depends on the value of . For numpy style it starts with the last dimension to search for a non-singleton dimension. For ILNumericsV4 the search starts with the first dimension (index #0).
This method is implemented for all common numeric element types, including and logical arrays.
This function may works inplace and may returns the same instance of .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.free``1(ILNumerics.Core.MemoryLayer.MemoryHandle,System.UInt32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Frees the handle for a memory region after use. This is for expert users in rare low-level scenarios only. Use the common array creation functions instead!
member.typeparam: Element type used to acquire the handle.
member.param: The handle pointing to the allocated memory region.
[Optional] Determines whether the memory is being returned to the OS. Default: false - the memory is cached into a pool for quick reusing.
The index of the device where the handles memory lives on. This must be the same device as the one used during allocation.

remarks.para: After having acquired the handle of a memory region on a device and having finished working with the memory make sure to release the memory back to the ILNumerics memory manager.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.ge(ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.fcomplex},ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.fcomplex})
member.summary: Elementwise 'GreaterOrEqual' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.ind2sub``6(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64},System.Int32)
member.summary: Computes dimensional indices from squential indices.
member.param: The input array providing the size, strides and element type to compute subscript indices for.
Sequential ('linear') indices into . n elements of arbitrary shape.
member.returns: A matrix [m, n], where m = .S.NumberOfElements and n = A.S.NumberOfDimensions. Indices for each dimension are stored in columns.

remarks.para: This function converts sequential element indices into subscript indices. Subscript indices specify the position of an element in by giving the position of the element in each dimension individually. Hence, n subscript indices are required to describe the element position in . In contrast to that, sequential indices specify the position of an element in by a single sequential index, where all elements are considered to be 'lined-up'. The sequential index is than simply the index of the element in the line.
The (virtual) lining-up of the elements in is performed in column major order. Note, that the order considered by is not related to the actual order of the elements as they are stored in memory.
If is not a vector its elements are read in column major order.

If the optional parameter is positive it specifies the number of output subscript dimensions to compute. This number can differ from the actual number of dimensions in . If is smaller than the number of dimensions in unspecified trailing dimensions of are virtually merged and the last column of subscript indices holds the indices into those merged dimension. Note, that in order to use these indices to address elements of subarray indexing must be performed in = .
If is larger than .S.NumberOfDimensions then subscripts in columns corresponding to virtual dimensions of will be '0'.
The matrix returned gives the subscripts for each element index in in rows. The matrix stores m rows of subscripts, corresponding to m elements in .

can contain values addressing non-existing elements in (indices out-of-range). These indices will produce out-of-range subscript indices also. In they may be used to grow the size of an array in a left-side index expression. does not give an error for out-of-range elements nor for negative values in ! The special meaning of latter (i.e.: counting from the end) is not considered here.
and are equivalent operations, inverting the results of the respective other function. Combining both functions creates a roundtrip and gives the original data.

member.exception: if has less than 1 dimension.
if or are null.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.isequal(ILNumerics.BaseArray,ILNumerics.BaseArray)
member.summary: Compares the number, shape, and type of elements of and and returns true if both are the same.
member.returns: True, if all elements and sizes of both arrays match; false otherwise.

remarks.para: Binary comparison is used on the elements. For floating point elements slight round-off errors will cause the comparison to fail! Use 'allall(abs(A - B) < tol)' or similar for floating point arrays instead. The same is recommended when performance is a critical factor: (just like the underlying function ) does not parallelize automatically and is recommended for simple, non-performance critical comparisons only.

If both arrays differ only in singleton dimensions but the types and (binary) values of all corresponding elements are equal the comparison can still succeed. Consider using additionally for a stricter comparisons including singleton dimensions.
This function is an alias for which overrides . In difference to latter the function does not perform reference comparison but the type and value of the elements are compared too.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.le(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'LowerOrEqual' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.lt(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.SByte},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.SByte})
member.summary: Elementwise 'LowerThan' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.max(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the maximum of elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] True: reduced singleton dimension is not removed from the output (default). False: the new singleton dimension is removed.
The index of the dimension to be reduced.
[Optional] Output: 0-based index values of the found elements along the working dimension. Default: (null) don't return the indices.
member.returns: New array with the same shape as except that the dimension specified by is reduced to length min(1,A.S[dim]) and removed if is false.

remarks.para: Empty arrays are handled in the same way as other shapes: the dimension specified by is reduced to 1. If A.S[dim] == 0 the s dimension length in the array returned will also be 0.
Scalar arrays: numpy scalars give a numpy scalar (0 dim) as output.

Special floating point values (for floating point element types): positive and negative infinity are handled in the regular way. NaN ('not a number') values are ignored. If all elements in a working dimension are NaN, NaN is returned as result in the corresponding output element.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If is null on entry (default) no indices are computated (may or may not decreasing the computational effort of completing this function).

Stability: if is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same minimum/maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined. It may point to the first or any other element storing the smallest / largest value returned from the working dimension. Thus, Min() and Max() are unstable regarding the index output argument!

member.exception: If A.S[dim] == 0 and was false.

Special floating point values (for floating point element types): positive and negative infinity are handled in the regular way. NaN ('not a number') values are ignored. If all elements in a working dimension are NaN, NaN is returned as result in the corresponding output element.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If is null on entry (default) no indices are computated (may or may not decreasing the computational effort of completing this function).

Stability: if is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same minimum/maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined. It may point to the first or any other element storing the smallest / largest value returned from the working dimension. Thus, Min() and Max() are unstable regarding the index output argument!

member.exception: If A.S[dim] == 0 and was false.

member.summary: Computes the (flattened, row-major) sequential index and value of the element with the maximum value in .
member.param: Array to compute the maximum for. This is not altered.
[Optional] index of the maximum value. Default: (null) the index is not returned.
[Optional] iteration order for the flattened sequential indices. Default: .
[Optional] determins how NaN values are handled for floating point element types. Ignored for integer elements. Defaul: (true) ignores NaNs.
member.returns: Scalar array with the maximum value in A.

remarks.para: See for getting the maximum values along a specific dimension.

The functions 'max','min','maxall','minall' give all similar results between the framework APIs (ILNumericsV4/Matlab(R) / numpy) but show individual behavior regarding the handling of floating point NaN values and iteration order. The value of 'true' for corresponds to the behavior of ILNumerics version 4/ Matlab(R). Only if all elements in are the value of the result will also be NaN. This is the default.

The value of 'false' for gives the numpy behavior: NaN values take precedence over non-NaN values. If one element in the set of values is NaN the result will also be NaN. This is the default behavior for such functions defined as [numpy API] extension methods on the array classes.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.meshgrid(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Create two matrices for evaluation and visualization of 2 dimensional functions over a 2d grid.
member.param: [Output, Optional]: if on entry is not null it holds the values for the Y dimension on return.
member.returns: X values matrix along the values of . Corresponding values for Y are returned in .

remarks.para: The matrices returned can conveniently be used to evaluate and visualize functions of 2 variables over a grid of (X Y) positions.

Note that the X dimension goes along the rows, while the second dimension is considered the columns! This deviates from the common intuition and the actual storage order of matrix elements (i.e.: first dimension along the columns and 2nd dimension along the rows). The reason for it is the convenience this order gives for plotting purposes: In most plots the X axis is expected to run horizontaly.

member.exception: If or is null.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.min(ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.fcomplex},ILNumerics.BaseArray{ILNumerics.fcomplex},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Gives the minimum of corresponding elements from and . Recognizes NaN values.
member.param: [Optional] specifies how to deal with NaN values in or . Default: (true) prefer non-NaN values if possible.
member.returns: Result of operating elements of and elementwise.

remarks.para: Handling of NaN values: is true (default). For floating point element types and if one of the elements to compare is the other element is returned. If both elements are the element from is returned.
If is false the result is if at least one of the elements is NaN. If both elements are NaN than the first element is returned.

Scalar arrays: numpy scalars give a numpy scalar (0 dim) as output.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If is null on entry (default) no indices are computated (may or may not decreasing the computational effort of completing this function).

Stability: if is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same minimum/maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined. It may point to the first or any other element storing the smallest / largest value returned from the working dimension. member.summary: Computes the (flattened, row-major) sequential index and value of the element with the minimum value in .
member.param: Array to compute the minimum for. This is not altered.
[Optional] index of the minimum value. Default: (null) the index is not returned.
[Optional] iteration order for the flattened sequential indices. Default: .
[Optional] determins how NaN values are handled for floating point element types. Ignored for integer elements. Defaul: (true) ignores NaNs.
member.returns: Scalar array with the minimum value in A.

remarks.para: See for getting the minimum values along a specific dimension.

The functions 'min','min','minall','minall' give all similar results between the framework APIs (ILNumericsV4/Matlab(R) / numpy) but show individual behavior regarding the handling of floating point NaN values and iteration order. The value of 'true' for corresponds to the behavior of ILNumerics version 4/ Matlab(R). Only if all elements in are the value of the result will also be NaN. This is the default.

The value of 'false' for gives the numpy behavior: NaN values take precedence over non-NaN values. If one element in the set of values is NaN the result will also be NaN. This is the default behavior for such functions defined as [numpy API] extension methods on the array classes.

The value of 'true' for corresponds to the behavior of ILNumerics version 4/ Matlab(R). Only if all elements in are the value of the result will also be NaN. This is the default.

The value of 'false' for gives the numpy behavior: NaN values take precedence over non-NaN values. If one element in the set of values is NaN the result will also be NaN. This is the default behavior for such functions defined as [numpy API] extension methods on the array classes.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.neq(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'UnEqualTo' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.New``1(System.UInt64,System.UInt32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Provides memory / T[] / a device buffer for the current thread. This is for expert users and rare low-level scenarios only. Use the common array creation functions instead!
member.typeparam: Element type, specifies the type and size of elements.
member.param: Number of elements which must at least fit into the memory region.
[Optional] Index of the device owning the memory. Default: 0 is the host device.
[Optional] Flag determining whether the memory should be initialized to zero. Default: do not clear.
member.returns: The returned will be a to a region on the main (virtual) memory, a to the managed heap or a on an OpenCL device.

remarks.para: This function attempts to acquire the requested chunk of memory from the memory pool of the specified device. Only if no matching region was found, memory is allocated from the low level allocation functions offered by the device.

This function supports the utilization of memory regions in a C style manner: user have to manage memory explicitly and manually. Instead of using this function it is recommended to use the common ILNumerics array creation functions to create and work with ILNumerics arrays. which do not require to create, clean up or to pool memory manually. ILNumerics function rules do all this automatically. Thus, manual memory management is left to a few, very specific situations only.

Depending on the type category the memory handle returned references one of the following memory types:
T is struct / ValueType: memory is allocated on the unmanaged heap. There is no inherent size limitation. Access to the memory is done by means of the property. Users are responsible to correctly deal with such pointers. All risks of unsafe code apply.
T is class / reference type: the function allocates an .NET on the managed heap. Access is done by first casting the memory handle returned to the concrete type of and then using the property to acquire the T[] array.
if is greater than 0 the handle returned will be a to an OpenCL device. For shared virtual memory devices (SVM), however, such buffers will be backed with a corresponding region of memory on the native virtual memory manager managed heap. It is this complexity which leads to the suggestion to not use this method of manual memory management ('New' and 'free') unless really necessary and unless you know what you are doing.
Attempting to access the on a native handle generates an exception.
Attempting to access the on a ManagedHostHandle{T} generates an exception.

MemoryHandles are critical handles. Disposal is guaranteed by critical execution regions and the GC. However, users should dispose the handle to free the memory region immediately after use. Use for disposing memory handles.

member.exception: on failed attempts to allocate a memory region on the specified device.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.or(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'Or' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.permute``1(ILNumerics.BaseArray{``0},ILNumerics.InArray{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Reorder dimensions of n-dimensional array .
member.param: New dimension order. The order of the zero-based indices of the original dimensions specify the target arrays shape.
member.returns: Array with reordered dimensions.
member.remarks:
will not change. A new array is created, having the dimensions rearranged in the order specified by .
The length of must match the number of dimensions in A: A.S.NumberOfDimensions == dim.Length.
In version 5 became more efficient since no elements must be copied for a permutation of the dimensions. The resulting array may not expose any common storage layout, though. Thus, subsequent operations handling the result may have to perform a copy nevertheless.
member.exception: If the number of elements in and the number of elements for the new dimensions specified by do not match or if any index of a dimension from is missing in list of elements in .

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.poly(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Single},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Single})
member.summary: Polynomial evaluation
member.param: Vector of coefficients of the polynomial
Position where the polynomial is to be evaluated. The position may be either a scalar, a vector or a matrix.

example.code: //Evaluation of the polynomial 1+x+2.1 x + x^2+3x^3 at (1,1,1) Array<float> y = ILMath.poly(ILMath.array<float>(1.0, 2.1, 1.0, 3.0),ILMath.ones<float>(3, 1));

member.returns: The value of a polynomial of degree d at position x, with d=c.lenght-1
member.remarks: If the input position is an array, the evaluation will be done elementwise

member.summary: Computes the product of all elements of .
member.returns: Scalar array with the product of all elements of .

remarks.para: The operation is efficiently performed on all elements of the input array .
The operation is performed in multiple threads, according to the current settings of .
The input array is not altered.

This operation returns a scalar array, regardless of the shape of . The number of dimensions of the scalar returned depends on the setting of . If is empty the scalar value returned corresponds to the default value of the element datatype. For numerical element types the default value is 0. For boolean / logical elements the default is false.

member.summary: Reinterpret the elements of A as elements of type . Expand or shrink the array size accordingly.
member.returns: A new array with the element type , referencing the same memory as A.
member.remarks:
The cast is performed regardless of the way the individual elements of A are currently stored in memory. When using this method one must consider the endianness of the system, which can vary from machine to machine!
If is of equal size as the array returned will have the same size and striding as A.
If the size of is smaller than the size of multiple elements of A are collapsed into a corresponding output element. Both sizes must match so that multiple element instances of fit exactly into a single element. The dimension where elements in A are stored continously in memory is shrinked by the fraction of the element size difference.
Otherwise, if the input elements size is larger than the size of a new trailing dimension is added, containing the newly extracted component from the larger input elements. In this case, the array returned has the same size than A, padded with a trailing dimension and the new dimension's length equals the number of fitting exactly into .
member.exception: if the sizes of the types requested do not match or if the storage layout of A is not appropriate.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.size(System.Int64[])
member.summary: Provides dimension lengths for operations expecting a size argument. Targets more than 7 dimensions.

remarks.para: This function is an alias for and returns a vector of elements.

For situations requiring high-performance execution you may consider using in order to create the required size vector once. Keep this size array around and reuse it. This prevents one from allocating additional, GC managed memory from the managed heap and may helps to increase the performance / to decrease GC activity. Otherwise, the 'params' (variable length argument) may puts pressure on the GC when used frequently in tight loops.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.sort(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sort elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] Determins the sorting direction. Default: (false) ascending.
The index of the working dimension or -1 for determining the working dimension automatically (default).
member.returns: New array with the same shape as .

remarks.para: The working dimension for = -1 depends on the value of . For numpy style it starts with the last dimension to search for a non-singleton dimension. For ILNumericsV4 the search starts with the first dimension (index #0).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.sort(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sort elements of along the specified dimension. Computes indices also.
member.param: [Output, optional] On return contains the indices required to sort the array.
[Optional] Determins the sorting direction. Default: (false) ascending.
The index of the working dimension or -1 for determining the working dimension automatically (default).
member.returns: New array with the same shape as .

remarks.para: The working dimension for = -1 depends on the value of . For numpy style it starts with the last dimension to search for a non-singleton dimension. For ILNumericsV4 the search starts with the first dimension (index #0).

If is of the same shape as (non-empty, non-scalar) on entry, its content is sorted with the values of A. Otherwise and if is not null and not of the same shape as the function will resize and fill it with zero based indices along the working dimension and sort these together with .

It is recommended to initialize with 0 or to indicate that the indices are required. If is scalar and is not null, any predefined value of is ignored and 0 is returned in . That means that initializing with 1 or any other scalar literal (for ease of use) does work also, as long as is not scalar.

member.summary: Sort data in A along dimension 'dim'
member.param: Input array: empty, scalar, vector or matrix

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.sort``3(ILNumerics.InArray{``0},ILNumerics.OutArray{``2},System.Int32,System.Boolean,ILNumerics.Core.Misc.KeyMapper{``0,``1})
member.summary: Generic bucket sort algorithm in A along arbitrary dimension
member.param: Input array: empty, scalar, vector or matrix
[Input/Output] The values in Indices will be returned in the same sorted order as the elements in A. This can be used to derive a permutation matrix of the sorted indices.
member.typeparam: Element type of values of A
Subelement type. For element type of string this would be 'char'
member.param: Instancce of an object of type ILKeyMapper. This object must be derived from ILKeyMapper{T,SubelementType} and match the generic argument . It will be used to split single elements into its subelements and map their content into bucket numbers. For all reference types except those of type string you will have to write your own ILKeyMapper class for that purpose.
member.returns: Sorted array of the same size as A

remarks.para: The data in A will be sorted using the bucket sort algorithm. Data along the dimension will get sorted independently. I.e., for dim = 0, columns are sorted independently.

This overload also returns an array 'Indices' which will hold the indices into the original elements after sorting. Therefore, the unsorted indices must be provided by the user on entry. Indices must not be null.

This generic version is able to sort arbitrary element types. Even user defined reference types can be sorted by specifying a user defined ILKeyMapper class instance. Also the type of Indices may be arbitrarily choosen. In difference to the regular sort function overload, Indices must manually be given to the function on entry. Elements in 'Indices' are sorted in the same order as the elements of A.

By using this overload you may use the same permutation matrix several times to reflect the manipulations done to A due multiple sort processes. The Indices given will directly be used for the sorting disregarding initial order.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.sub2ind``6(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.InArray{System.Int64})
member.summary: Computes sequential (linear) indices from dimensional indices.
member.param: The input array providing the size, strides and element type to compute the sequential indices for.
Dimensional index tuples into as m elements of n rows. Matrix [m, n].
member.returns: Vector [m] with sequential element indices into according to the subscript indices (rows) from .

remarks.para: This function converts subscript indices into sequential element indices. Subscript indices specify the position of an element in by giving the position of the element in each dimension individually. Hence, n subscript indices are required to describe a single element position in . In contrast to that, sequential indices specify the position of an element in by a single sequential index, where all elements are considered to be 'lined-up'. The sequential index is than simply the index of the element in the line.

The (virtual) lining-up of the elements in is performed in column major order. Note, that the order considered by and by is not related to the actual order of the elements as they are stored in memory.
If has fewer columns as dimensions exist in indices into unspecified dimensions are considered 0. The last column of may contains values as indices into the merged trailing dimensions of .

The vector returned gives the sequential index for each element specified as a row in . A sequential index corresponds to the 0-based index of the element after lining-up all elements of , starting at element 0 and walking along the array in column major order.

can contain values addressing non-existing elements in (indices out-of-range). These indices will produce invalid sequential indices and do not produce an error. Also, no error is generated for negative values in ! The special meaning of latter (i.e.: counting from the end) is not considered here.
and are equivalent operations, inverting the results of the respective other function. Combining both functions creates a roundtrip and gives the original data.

member.exception: if has less than 1 dimension.
if or are null.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.xor(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64},ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.UInt64})
member.summary: Elementwise 'Xor' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.summary: Elementwise 'Xor' comparison operator on two arrays.
member.returns: Logical array with the size broadcasted from and .

remarks.para:
General notes on binary broadcasting operators: The operation is performed elementwise on corresponding elements of and . The sizes of both input arrays must be broadcastable and determine the size of the resulting array. Note, that broadcasting is performed, regardless of the current setting of . However, the configuration affects the operation in the following ways:
If and have different number of dimensions, the array with fewer dimensions is (virtually) padded with singleton dimensions, until the number of dimensions of both arrays match. In the singleton dimensions are added to the end of dimensions. For singletons are padded to the start, such that here, broadcasting aligns the last dimensions.
: Result values of integer element types T are clamped to the natural range of the interger type. I.e.: there will be no 'wrapping around' when exceeding the upper or lower limits of the natural value range of the integer type. Also, the operation may be performed by utilizing precision floating point arithmetics and subsequently casting the result to the desired integer value. For no such precautions exist and the result of the binary operation is exactly the same as for operating the elements as System types (and as in numpy itself).

member.name: M:ILNumerics.ILMath.gammaLog(ILNumerics.InArray{System.Double})
member.summary: Evaluates the natural logarithm of the Gamma function at a given point. For more details about this function, see Wikipedia - Gamma function and Wolfram MathWorld - Log Gamma function.
member.param: The point where the function is evaluated.
member.returns: log(gamma()) with gamma() = from 0 to ∞ ∫(t^(-1)exp(-t))dt.

list.item: The value of the Gamma function can be found simply using the exponential of the value found from the function. Example: exp(gammaLog(10.0)) will give the value of the gamma function at 10.0.
In this particular implementation the positive real numbers are supported.
If the given point is negative the return value will be double.NaN.
If the given point is zero the return value will be double.PositiveInfinity.
If any of the given points is double.NaN or double.IsInfinity is true, an ArgumentException will be thrown.
If the input array is empty, an empty array will be returned.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.numpy.max(ILNumerics.BaseArray{System.Double},ILNumerics.OutArray{System.Int64},System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the maximum of elements of along the specified dimension.
member.param: [Optional] True: reduced singleton dimension is not removed from the output (default). False: the new singleton dimension is removed.
The index of the dimension to be reduced.
[Optional] Output: 0-based index values of the found elements along the working dimension. Default: (null) don't return the indices.
member.returns: New array with the same shape as except that the dimension specified by is reduced to length min(1,A.S[dim]) and removed if is false.

remarks.para: Empty arrays are handled in the same way as other shapes: the dimension specified by is reduced to 1. If A.S[dim] == 0 the s dimension length in the array returned will also be 0.
Scalar arrays: numpy scalars give a numpy scalar (0 dim) as output.

Special floating point values (for floating point element types): positive and negative infinity are handled in the regular way. NaN ('not a number') values are ignored. If all elements in a working dimension are NaN, NaN is returned as result in the corresponding output element.

If the optional output parameter is not null on entry the function computes and returns the indices in of the values returned. Thus, has the same shape as the return array. If the storage of on entry is sufficient (i.e.: large enough and not shared with other arrays) it will be directly used for storing the indices and I is reshaped as required. Otherwise, a new array is created and returned. In order to safe the index computation null can be provided as which is the default.

If is requested and multiple elements along the working dimension in have the same maximum value it is undefined which element is 'picked' for the output. Hence, in this case the corresponding value in is undefined and may point to the first or any other occurrence of the value returned from the working dimension.

member.exception: If A.S[dim] == 0 and was false.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.numpy.put``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.Mutable{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},ILNumerics.InArray{``0},ILNumerics.PutModes)
member.summary: Replaces elements of with at positions given by sequential (i.e.: flatten, row-major) .
member.typeparam: Element type of indices. Must be numeric.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be replaced.
Index array. The shape is ignored. Values must be numeric and are read in row-major order.
Values array. The shape is ignored. Values are read in row-major order.
[Optionl] Specifies how to handle index values in which are out-of-range. Default: error.

remarks.para: This function has a similar effect as doing A.flat[indices] = values in numpy. However, in ILNumerics the iterator returned from A.flat is read-only. Use as a replacement.

Note that the values in are considered sequential indices, i.e. they correspond to the element position in a flattened array, where the flattening is performed in row-major order. For performance reasons and if . is not A is converted to row-major storage layout first and remains in row-major storage after the function returns. Note further, that the conversion happens proactively, and is not rolled back in case of errors during the iteration.
Elements of can be negative, which corresponds to indexing from the end of flattened .
Repeated values in lead to only the last corresponding value in to be stored at the respective position in .

If has more elements than are indices provided in superfluent values are ignored. No exception is thrown in this case. If has fewer elements than indices are provided in existing values are repeated as necessary.

The parameter determines what happens with indices laying outside of the bounds of A. The default value of throws an in this case. Two other options exist which bring the index back into the valid range: computes the modulus, limits the indices to the allowed range. Note that negative indices behave as usual (counting from the end of A) for modes and only.
requires the element type of to be value types (struct, commonly numeric).

member.exception: if is and any element in is out of the allowed range of [-A.S.NumberOfElements...>= A.].

member.name: M:ILNumerics.numpy.repeat``7(ILNumerics.Core.Arrays.ConcreteArray{``0,``1,``2,``3,``4,``5},ILNumerics.BaseArray{``6},System.Nullable{System.UInt32})
member.summary: Repeat elements along a flattened array or a specific axis.
member.typeparam: Element type of . Must be an integer type.
member.param: The array storing the elements to be repeated.
[Optional] The working dimension. Default: (null) flatten A and repeat all values along dimension #0.

remarks.para: This function repeats elements of along a single dimension. By default, where no is defined is reshaped to a vector in row-major order and all elements are repeated according to . Otherwise, if an was specified, repetitions are performed along that dimension only. In this case, the array returned has the same shape as , except that the working dimension is enlarged.

The shape of is ignored. Its values give the counts for each element along the axis . Values must be numeric, positive integers and are read in row-major order. If has exactly one element all elements along the working dimension of are repeated by the same number. Alternatively, the length of must match A.S[axis] to specify individual repetition counts for each element along the working dimension. Thus, if is null (default) can be a scalar or an array with 'A.S.NumberOfElements == repeats.S.NumberOfElements'.
This function returns a new array and does not alter or any input parameters.

member.exception: if any of the or is null

if points to a virtual dimension; if is not a numeric array, is of a shape which is not broadcastable to the length of the working dimension or contains elements which are not convertible to positive integer values;

member.name: T:ILNumerics.ArrayStyles
member.summary: Options of array semantics. This enum is used to switch the behavior of and Co. between ILNumerics version 4 (Matlab, Julia, etc.) and numpy mode.

member.name: F:ILNumerics.ArrayStyles.ILNumericsV4
member.summary: Default indexing and array styles. Handles subarray / indexing expressions in the tradional way, similar to Matlab(R), octave and ILNumerics prior version 5. All arrays exist as matrices (i.e.: have 2 or more dimensions, even vectors and scalars).

remarks.para: When this setting is selected, unspecified trailing dimensions are (virtually) substituted with '0', addressing the first element in the dimension (Matlab(R) style subarrays).
All arrays are created as matrices having at least 2 dimensions.
Addressing the last dimension with ":" or in subarray expressions leads to a reshaping of the array and merging unspecified subsequent dimensions into the last dimension (linear index expansion).
Arrays can be expanded, parts of arrays can be removed in subarray/ indexing expressions.
The default storage order for new arrays is .

member.name: F:ILNumerics.ArrayStyles.numpy
member.summary: Array handling and subarray / indexing expressions are handled similar to numpy.

remarks.para: When this setting is selected, unspecified trailing dimensions are (virtually) substituted with ':', addressing all of the trailing dimension ('ellipsis', numpy indexing).
Arrays can have less than 2 dimensions. 1-dim vectors and 0-dim scalars are supported.
Indexing parameters contribute to the dimensionality of the result. For scalars as index parameters this leads to a reduction of dimensions of the result.
All indices provided must be in the range of valid indices for each dimension. No linear index expansion is supported!
Arrays cannot be expanded, no parts of arrays can be removed in subarray/ indexing expressions.
The default storage order for new arrays is .

member.name: P:ILNumerics.MatFile.Item(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves an array from this MatFile instance or replaces it.
member.param: The name of the array to retrieve or replace.

remarks.para: The 'get' accessor is provided for compatibility reasons only. It may be removed in a future version! Use one of the typed retrieval functions or instead.
For get access the name must exist as key in the container. Use the MatFile.Keys property to get a list of all names if needed

For set access, the name given must not be null or empty. It cannot be one of the ReservedKeywords. If the name allready exist in the collection as name, the array currently assigned to it will be replaced. If the value is null, the current array will be removed from the list. If the name does not already exist, the new array will be added and assigned to this name.

Restrictions on array names: Matlab allows variables to have names of maximum length 63. Longer names are abbreviated. Names must start with a letter and contain only digits, (ASCII) letters or underscores '_'.

member.exception: If the name violates a Matlab naming rule.

member.name: M:ILNumerics.Scope.Enter(System.Nullable{ILNumerics.ArrayStyles})
member.summary: Begins an artificial scope block within a local function, determine the array style.
member.param: The valid within the scope block. A non-null value will be used within the scope block as current array style.
member.returns: The new scope object.

remarks.para: The Scope class plays an important role for the ILNumerics memory management. When writing functions in ILNumerics, Scope is used to define blocks of artificial scopes for local function blocks. ILNumerics ensures that no memory is left as garbage after the scope block is left. Furthermore, it garantees that input arrays are kept alive during the execution of the block. By following these ILNumerics function rules ILNumerics is able to optimize the execution of the algorithm regarding execution speed and memory footprint.

If a value other than null is given for the value of is modified for the operations within this scope block. After the scope is left, the old setting is reliably restored. If null is provided the current setting of is not touched.
Several overloads exist allowing to specify one or multiple arrays together with the array style setting.

example.para: The examples demonstrates a custom function in ILNumerics. It demonstrates the use of an artificial scope block to temporarily change the array style for the thread.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Settings.SaturateIntegerOps
member.summary: True: instruct integer array operations to saturate (clamp) results to the limits of the respective data type. False: perform wrapping around on overflow. Default: (null) the behavior depends on the setting of for the current thread.

member.name: P:ILNumerics.Settings.ArrayStyle
member.summary: Controls the way nd-arrays work. Affects the shape of arrays, the default storage order and the handling of subarray / indexing expressions. Thread static. Default: .

remarks.para: This settings controls the way arrays work. Valid options are and .

This affects the number and shape of vectors and scalars, of arrays returned from subarray expressions / indexing, the handling of unspecified trailing dimensions in indexing expressions, the default storage order, (saturating or clipping) behavior for integer operations, and others.

The default value is . It corresponds to the ILNumerics version 4, Matlab(R), octave and Julia systems. The setting of corresponds to numpys ndarrays. See for a comprehensive list of aspects affected by this setting.
Other settings which directly derive their value from the value of are: and .

This setting is controlled on a thread level! Modifications affect the current thread only and do not change the behavior in other threads! This enables one to safely switch between individual styles in multithreaded algorithms.
New threads are initialized with a value for according to .
In order to set to a valid license for the ILNumerics.numpy module is required.
